meanings.meaning: A priest is someone who offers sacrifices to God and stands between the people and Him. In Israel, the job was given to Aaron's family, from the tribe of Levi.
A priest in other religions is a person who offers sacrifices and does sacred acts for a false god. He acts as a go-between for people and the god they worship, such as Dagon.
A prophet is a person who speaks for God. God gives him a message, and he tells it to the people in God's name, sometimes about what will happen later.
A false prophet is someone who pretends to speak for God but does not. He is an impostor who fools people with his own made-up messages.
The Prophets are the writings of the prophets, the messages God gave through them. Together with the Law of Moses, they make up the Scriptures of the Old Testament.
The side of the head between the eye and the ear. In this verse it is the part of the head that a tent peg is driven through.
The holy house in Jerusalem built for worshiping God. It was also called the house of the Lord, and people went there to pray and offer sacrifices.
A building set apart for worshiping a god. Many nations built temples for their false gods and idols, and people gathered there to worship them.
A disciple is someone who learns from a teacher and follows him. In the Bible, it mostly means a follower of Jesus, who believes His teaching and tries to live like Him.
An elder was a leader with authority who was respected by the people. Elders governed and judged among God's people, and the title was later used for leaders in the church.
An offering is a gift given to God in worship, like crops, animals, or silver and gold. It could show thanks, sorrow for sin, or giving oneself to God.
Breaking God's law or disobeying what He commands. It can be doing something wrong or failing to do what is right, in a person's actions and in the heart.
In 'sin offering,' a sacrifice given to God because of sin.
The name of a desert, or wilderness, between Elim and Rephidim, near the Red Sea, where the Israelites traveled and camped. This name is not the same as the word sin that means doing wrong.
An angel is a spirit being who serves God. The word means "messenger," and angels carry God's messages, obey His commands, and help people, though some angels sinned and were judged.
The Holy Spirit is God Himself, the third Person of the Trinity, who is one with the Father and the Son. He helps, teaches, strengthens and comforts God's people.
A being without a body, such as an angel or a demon. Good spirits serve God, and bad or unclean spirits are evil.
The part of a person that is not the body, the inner life or soul. It can also mean a person's feeling or attitude, like a spirit of grace.
A psalm is a sacred song or poem written to praise God and worship Him. The Bible's Book of Psalms gathers 150 of these songs, which were used in worship.
An Israelite is a person who comes from Israel, who was also called Jacob. The Israelites were Jacob's descendants, also called Hebrews.
A raised structure of earth, stone, or wood covered with metal, where gifts were offered to God. Some altars were also built as memorials to mark a place where God appeared.
When God blesses someone, He gives good gifts like help or success. People bless others by wishing them good, and a blessed person is seen as fortunate.
When people bless God, they praise Him and thank Him for His kindness, giving Him the honor He deserves.
To bless food or a cup is to speak to God over it, giving Him thanks before it is shared. The cup of blessing was a feast cup treated this way.
A tribe is a large group of families who all came from one ancestor. The twelve tribes of Israel were the families that came from the twelve sons of Jacob.
In these verses, tribe means a wider group of people from anywhere in the world, not only Israel's twelve tribes. "Every tribe" means people of all kinds of families and groups.
Wisdom is knowing the best goals to aim for and the best ways to reach them. It means using what you know with good judgment, and it can also mean skill or learning.
An apostle is someone sent out with a message. It mostly means the twelve disciples Jesus chose to preach the gospel, but Paul, other messengers, and Jesus are also called apostles.
A sacrifice is something offered to God, often an animal laid on an altar, to worship Him, thank Him, or ask Him to forgive sin. To sacrifice means to make such an offering.
A sacrifice can also mean giving up something you value for the sake of something more important.
An idol is an image or object that people worship in place of the true God. Anything that gets the love and worship that belong only to God can also be called an idol.
Levites were descendants of Levi, one of Israel's tribes. The name usually means the men of Levi who were not priests, who were set apart to serve God at His sanctuary and help the priests.
A covenant is a solemn agreement between two sides. When God makes one, He gives His serious promise and also tells people what they must do to keep it.
A covenant between people is a serious agreement, often made before God as witness. Both sides promise to do something, and the promise must be kept.
Right and fair in what one does and chooses, living by God's ways. It describes a person who obeys God, and also acts or commands that are just and good.
A throne is a high, special chair where a king or other leader sits on important occasions. It shows his power and honor, and God's throne is the place of His rule.
Sometimes "throne" means a king's power to rule, not just his chair. To sit on the throne means to rule as king.
Faith is trusting that something is true and can be relied on. In the Bible it means trusting God and what He has said.
Sometimes "the faith" means the truth of the good news about Jesus and the kingdom of God, which believers hold on to and teach.
Faith can also mean faithfulness, or staying loyal to someone. To "break faith" with God is to be unfaithful to Him.
A wild, open stretch of land where few or no people live and nothing is farmed. It could be dry and empty, but it could also have grass where sheep and cattle graze.
A wild, empty place where no one lives or farms. Cities that were once lived in can become like this when they are left abandoned and ruined.
A dry, empty land with nothing to give. God asks if He has been like this to Israel, a place with no care or help.
A special meal with plenty of good food, shared with guests. People held feasts to welcome visitors or to celebrate happy events, and sometimes added music and dancing.
A holy festival set for a appointed time. God's people gathered before Him to worship and to remember what He had done.
A palace is the home of a king or other ruler. It was often a large, strong group of buildings, with halls, courtyards, and gardens inside a wall.
In 1 Chronicles 29:19, David uses the word for the temple, the grand house for God, which Solomon would build.
A huge wooden boat Noah built at God's command. It was covered with pitch, a sticky waterproof coating, and it kept Noah's family and the animals safe during the Flood.
The holy wooden chest of God's promise to His people. It was made of acacia wood and held the flat stones with God's commands written on them.
A Pharisee belonged to a group of Jews in Jesus' time. They followed the law of Moses and the old traditions very strictly, and they often thought they were better than other people.
Living in a right way, with a heart devoted to God and honest, fair actions that match His law. When used of God, it means His perfect goodness, justice, and faithfulness.
Being right with God. This comes from God's undeserved kindness when a person trusts in Jesus Christ, who always obeyed God perfectly.
To reign is to rule as a king, holding the highest power over a people or land. It also means the time a king rules, and when the LORD reigns, He is the supreme ruler.
Grain is the seed of plants like wheat and barley, used for food. The word can mean one tiny seed or a whole crop of these seeds, even while still growing in the field.
A day of rest from work, usually the seventh day of the week. God set it apart as holy, and He gave it to Israel as part of His laws.
A whole year of rest, kept every seventh year by the Israelites. In this year the land was to rest, as a time set apart for the LORD.
An official is a person who holds an office, a job of trust and authority. Officials carry out the duties of that position.
A king's secretary or official writer who wrote his letters and official orders and sometimes handled money. Later, scribes copied God's Law and taught it to people.
In New Testament times, a scribe was a teacher who copied and explained God's Law. Scribes were usually linked with the Pharisees, and their added traditions often hid the meaning of the Law.
A blessing is a good gift that brings happiness, or a prayer or wish asking God's favor for someone. A person can be a blessing when God uses them to bring good.
A blessing can be words of thanks and praise given to God. People bless God when they thank Him for His kindness and honor Him.
To honor someone as God by bowing down, praying, or serving. True worship belongs only to God, and giving it to anything else is idolatry.
Giving honor, love, and respect to God through acts like prayer and thanksgiving. People also gave this kind of honor to false gods, which the Bible calls idolatry.

A smooth liquid squeezed from olives, one of the country's most valuable products. The Hebrews used it for cooking, lamp light, medicine, worship offerings, and anointing, which means pouring it on someone.
A vehicle with two wheels pulled by horses. It was used mostly in war, but sometimes for travel or to honor a person, and a nation's strength could be judged by how many it had.
A burnt offering was a gift to God made by burning an animal on an altar. The animals were clean ones, such as cattle, sheep, or goats.
A commandment is an order or rule given by someone with authority. In the Bible it is often something God commands His people to obey, like the Ten Commandments He gave Moses on Mount Sinai.
To obey is to do what someone in charge tells you to do, and to stay away from what they forbid. It means to follow their commands and accept their authority.
Property or land that a parent or ancestor passes down to children. In the Bible, God also gives land to His people as their inheritance.
God's own people, who belong to Him as His special possession.
A valuable gift or blessing that God gives to those who belong to Him, such as salvation and the kingdom of heaven. Believers receive it because they are His children.
Iniquity is wrongdoing, or anything done against God's law. It can mean a sinful act, or the wicked and unjust way a person lives.
A witness is a person who saw or knows about something and tells what is true, or a thing that stands as proof. A heap of stones could be a witness too.
An enclosed piece of ground where grapevines are planted and grown to produce grapes.
The good news about Jesus Christ: that God saves people and rescues them from their sin through Him. The word itself means "good news" or "glad news."
Wrath is very strong anger, like rage or fury. When it is God's wrath, it is His holy and fair anger against sin, and it can bring a just punishment for wrongdoing.
A time when there is not enough food for the people of a land. It can happen when rain or river floods fail, or when insects eat the crops.
A great lack of something other than food. In Amos, God speaks of people being starved for hearing His words instead of for bread.
Not pure in the way God's law required, such as after touching a dead body, so a special washing was needed. Unclean animals were ones the Israelites were forbidden to eat.
Evil or wicked. An unclean spirit is a wicked spirit, also called a demon.
The Ammonites were the people descended from Ammon, a son of Lot. They lived east of the Jordan River, worshipped idols, and were often enemies of Israel.
Grace is God's free and undeserved kindness and love. He gives it as a gift, not a reward, and every good thing He gives comes from it.
Grace can mean beauty or loveliness, a pleasing quality in a person's looks or words that makes others admire them.
Grace can be a kind and generous spirit, a good quality that God works in believers' hearts. It shows up in loving acts, like giving freely to others.
An oath is a solemn promise or statement made by appealing to God, or to something sacred. Some oaths include a curse on anyone who does a certain thing.
Being saved or rescued from danger, enemies, or harm. In the New Testament it especially means God saving people from sin and death through Jesus, including forgiveness of sins.
A synagogue was a place where Jewish people met to worship, and the word also means the group that gathered there. They came together to read the Law and the Prophets.
A short saying that is often repeated and teaches a truth or wise lesson learned from life.
A hard-to-understand saying, like a riddle or parable. A listener has to think carefully to see what it means.
A byword: a name or example people repeat to mock someone. To become a proverb means to be an object of shame and scorn.
A saying or phrase that people often repeat and everyone knows. It may be a common line that people quote, even if it is not a wise lesson.
A Gentile is anyone who is not a Jew. The Jews used this word for all the other nations, who did not share Israel's worship and special place as God's people.
A psalmist is someone who writes songs about God or faith. The name is used especially for David and the other writers of the psalms in the Bible.
A scroll is a long sheet of paper or parchment, which is a writing material, with words written on it. It is rolled up into a roll.
To pour or rub oil on a person or thing to set it apart for God's special use, as with priests, kings, prophets, and holy objects. "The anointed" means someone chosen this way.
To rub oil on the body, as people did to refresh themselves, to show kindness to a guest, or to care for the sick. Not putting on oil was a sign of mourning.
To be chosen and set apart by God through the Holy Spirit, not by pouring oil. The promised Deliverer, the Messiah, is called the Anointed One, and Jesus is that One.
A place where a dead person's body is laid. Among the Hebrews, tombs were often caves or rooms cut into solid rock, and the entrance was usually closed with a large stone.
A plague is a terrible trouble or sickness that strikes people. In the Bible, God often sends it as a punishment or judgment, like the plagues on Egypt.
The holy writings that God gave through people He chose, so that His message would be kept. In the Bible, the word mostly means the Old Testament, and today it means the whole Bible.
One particular passage or verse from the holy writings, like a single text that is quoted or pointed to.
The sacred tent Moses built as God's dwelling place, where God promised to meet with Israel. It could be moved from place to place and was used for worship and sacrifice.

Tabernacles are booths, which are simple, temporary shelters. The Feast of Tabernacles was a yearly autumn feast after the harvest, when people lived in booths for seven days to remember Israel's long years in tents.
A portable shrine, which is a special holy place that can be carried around. This one held the image of Moloch, a false god the people worshiped.
A person who is owned by someone else and forced to work for him. A slave was not free to leave.
Someone who is ruled by a power and surrenders to it, such as a slave to anger, greed, or strong drink. In the Bible, a person can also be a slave to obedience.
To scatter a liquid or fine bits of something, like blood, oil, water, or dust, so it falls in small drops or pieces. It can also mean to cleanse or make pure.
A yearly Jewish feast that remembers how God passed over the houses of the Israelites when He struck the firstborn of Egypt. It also means the lamb eaten at that feast.
A vow is a serious promise, most often made to God, to do something or to give something up. Once it was made, it was to be kept.
A vow can also be a serious promise one person makes to another, like a king's promise to a woman, with the LORD called on as witness.
Beloved describes someone who is greatly loved and very dear to the heart. It can also be a name for a person who is loved this way.
A sweet-smelling mix of spices and plant sap that was burned as an offering, or the smoke it made. It was burned in worship and stood for prayer.
People who belong to God and are called to live for Him. In the Bible, the word is used for God's people and for believers in Christ, who are called to live holy lives.
A holy place set apart for God. In the Bible it can mean the tabernacle, the temple, or heaven, and also the sacred inner room where the ark was kept.
A place of safety and protection. Isaiah says God Himself will be this kind of shelter.
A statute is a law or rule that someone in authority commands people to follow. In the Bible, God's statutes are His commands, and a leader can also set one for the people.
The Chaldeans were the people of Chaldea, also called the Babylonians. In the Bible the word can mean the people who lived there, or their army.
An olive is a small fruit from the olive tree, a common tree in Palestine. It turns nearly black when ripe, and people valued it mostly for its oil.
The firstborn is the first child born in a family, or the first male animal born. Under God's Law for Israel, firstborn sons and male animals belonged to God, and sons got a double share.
Firstborn can mean the most excellent, honored, or highest one, not just the oldest. God uses it for Israel, David, and Christ to show a special place of honor.
Firstborn can mean the most extreme of something. The firstborn of the poor are the most miserable of the poor, and the firstborn of death pictures a deadly, destructive power.
The people who live in Egypt, a land in Africa. A person from Egypt is called an Egyptian.
The Testimony is the two stone tablets with the Ten Commandments on them, kept in the ark of the covenant. Sometimes the word names the ark itself.
What a witness says about something, to show what happened or what is true. It can be true or false, like words spoken in court or about Jesus.
God's words and teachings, which show His will. The psalm writers love and obey these testimonies, and the gospel about Christ is also called the testimony.
To rebuke is to speak sharply to someone about a fault, or to scold. It can also mean to stop something with a strong command, or to punish for correction.
Chronicles are records of what happened, written down in the order it happened. In these verses, the Chronicles are official records of events during the kings' reigns.
To make something unclean or impure. In the Bible, people, places, or things can be defiled by sin, by touching what the law called unclean, or by a terrible wrong.
Refuge is shelter or protection from danger or trouble, or a safe place like a stronghold. To take refuge in God is to trust Him to keep you safe.
Cities of refuge were special cities set apart in Israel. A person who had killed someone without meaning to could run there to be safe.
Woe is deep sadness and trouble. It is also a cry used to warn that punishment or disaster is coming, or to say "how terrible for me!" when someone is sorrowful.
To perish is to die or be destroyed. It can also mean to be lost, to pass away, or to come to nothing.
A decree is an official order or law from someone with power, such as a king or God. To decree something is to command it or decide that it will happen.
An evil spirit that is against God. Demons can harm people, and they know Jesus is the Son of God.
A false god, also called a goat idol, that people worshipped by offering sacrifices to it instead of to God.
A loud horn, made of silver or a ram's horn, that priests blew to announce festivals, signal war, and join in praise. In Revelation, trumpets are also symbols.
An officer is a person given a job or position of duty, like a government, army, or church helper. The Bible uses the word loosely for many kinds of officials.
What still remains after the rest has been taken away, destroyed, or used up. In the Bible, it often means the small group of people who are still left.
An insect like a big grasshopper that can gather in huge groups and eat many plants. Some swarms were so thick they could hide the sun, and some people also ate locusts as food.
To tell what will happen in the future, or to speak God's message to people. It can also mean to teach about God and explain His word.
To give something to God as an act of worship, like a sacrifice, a gift, or a prayer. It is a way of presenting it to Him.
To fulfill is to carry out or finish something, such as a promise, a wish, a task, or a vow. It also means a time or a set of days has come to its end.
When used about prophecy, to fulfill means that what the prophets said long before really happened, just as they said it would.
A cloak is a loose, long outer piece of clothing worn over other clothes, usually without sleeves. Paul's cloak was a thick outer garment that protected him from the weather when he traveled.
To buy something or someone back by paying a price. In the Bible, God redeems His people by rescuing them from slavery, trouble, or sin, and Christ redeems people with His life.
A name for Abraham and his family line, the people of Israel. Foreigners often used it for them, and Israelites used it when speaking about themselves to foreigners.
The language spoken by the Hebrew people, the Israelites.
The whole Hebrew people as one holy community, held together by their religion rather than politics. Their family and tribe leaders spoke for them.
A group of people gathered together to worship God and learn about Him. In the New Testament it can mean the Christian Church as a whole, or one local group of believers.
The exodus was the great going out of the Israelites from Egypt under Moses. It was a great rescue, when God brought them out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm.
A payment that people are required to make to those in charge. It can be money or goods, like grain, and it is often used to support a government or a group.
A message about something that will happen in the future, given by someone God has informed. It can also mean preaching or teaching to guide people.
A book or written record of prophecies, or a history, like the prophecy of Ahijah. It is the written form of messages from a prophet.
An Aramean is a person from Aram, the land of the Syrians. The word can also describe things connected to Aram, such as its people or language.
Eternal means lasting forever, with no end. When it describes God, it also means He has always existed, with no beginning.
Wickedness is evil living that goes against God's rules. It can mean bad actions like sin and crime, or an evil heart that wants to do wrong.
To treat people cruelly and unfairly, such as by loading them with heavy burdens or hard work. Someone who is oppressed is weighed down by this harsh treatment.
A short story about everyday things that teaches a deeper truth. In the Bible, the word can also mean a wise saying or a hidden message that needs thinking about to understand.
A Philistine was a person from Philistia, an ancient coastal region in southern Palestine. In these verses, the word also describes that people's camps, leaders, and land.
The Canaanites were the many tribes who lived in the land of Canaan. They were descendants of Canaan, a son of Ham, and lived in the land before Israel arrived.
To baptize is to dip a person under water or sprinkle water on them as a holy ceremony. Some churches also give a name to a baby during this ceremony.
To baptize can also mean to make someone holy, setting them apart for a special purpose.
A sinner is someone who has broken God's law or disobeyed what He commands. The word often describes a person who keeps doing wrong and has not turned away from it.
The unseen place where people's souls go after they die. It can also mean the grave.
A strongly built place made to defend against enemies, like a fort or castle. The Bible also calls God a fortress because He keeps His people safe and protects them.
A forefather is an ancestor, a person from earlier in your family line. Often he lived a long time ago, many generations back.
Atonement is making things right so people can be at one with God again. In the Bible, a priest makes atonement with an offering to pay for a wrong.
Tenth means number ten in a list or order, coming right after the ninth. The Bible uses it for the tenth month, the tenth day, and the tenth hour.
A tenth is one of ten equal parts of something. In the Bible, it often means a tithe, which is a tenth part of a person's yearly crops or income.
Something that people or God hate and are disgusted by, such as evil acts, idols, and things that make people unclean. It can also mean the strong feeling of hatred itself.
A strong farm animal from the cattle family. Oxen pulled plows and loads, trampled grain, and were used for sacrifices, and they were very valuable to Israelite farmers.
A wild animal of the cattle family, not one kept on a farm. The Bible uses it as a picture of strength.
To feel sorrow for something wrong you have done and change your mind or your way of living because of it. When people repent of sin, they are sorry for it and ask forgiveness.
To consecrate is to set a person or thing apart for God and holy use. The Bible uses it for priests, altars, fields, animals, and whole groups of people.
In Isaiah, people consecrate themselves for a ritual in the groves, which are not for God. They set themselves apart for something they treat as sacred, and the LORD says they will perish.
A tough tribe of hill people descended from a man named Canaan. They lived in the hill country and later in fertile land east of the Jordan River, and Israel often fought them.
Land covered with growing plants where sheep, cattle, and other animals graze. As a verb, to pasture means to feed animals there, or for animals to eat there.
Presented as an act of worship, such as a sacrifice, incense, or a prayer. In the Bible these were offered to God, but sometimes to idols or demons.
Held out or given for someone to accept or refuse. A person could offer himself, as when he held out his back to be struck.
A wooden bar laid on the necks of work animals like oxen so they can pull a plow or load together. To yoke animals is to put this bar on them.
A pair of oxen joined together by a yoke. It can also mean the amount of land such a pair could plow in a day.
A picture of slavery, harsh rule, or a heavy burden. Breaking or removing the yoke means being set free, or sometimes refusing to obey an authority.
A place where money and valuable things are stored and kept safe. Public money was kept there and paid out when needed, and in the temple it was where gifts were received.

Oxen are strong, patient farm animals, a kind of cattle, that were very valuable. They plowed, pulled carts, carried loads, walked on grain to separate it from the stalks, and were used for sacrifices.
Sackcloth was rough, scratchy cloth made from dark goats' hair, the same kind used for making sacks. People wore it to show deep sadness or sorrow for their sins.
A gentle bird, a kind of pigeon, that nests in holes in rocks and can be tamed. The Bible uses it as a picture of peace, purity, and loving care.
A loving name for someone who is dear, pure, and gentle. In the Song of Solomon, the groom calls his bride "my dove."
To make clean, such as by washing away dirt, sin, or guilt. In the Bible it can also mean to heal a disease, or to make someone or something ceremonially clean for God.
A Moabite is a person from the nation that came from Moab, the son of Lot. Used as a describing word, it means belonging to the Moabites, like a Moabite city or Moabite women.
To put someone to death by nailing his hands and feet to a cross.
To crush the power of something, like sinful wants, so it no longer rules over you.
The devil is Satan, the great enemy of God and of people. His name means "slanderer," and he tempts people to do evil and accuses them.
Sometimes the word is used for a very wicked person, such as Judas Iscariot, who acts like the devil.
A threshing floor was a flat, hard patch of ground, often on a windy hilltop, where people separated grain from the straw. A village might share one, and farmers took turns using it.
Threshing means beating or crushing harvested grain to knock it out of the straw. People used oxen's feet or a heavy tool with rollers and sharp iron teeth.
Fasting means choosing not to eat for a time. People did it as a religious act, to show sadness, humility, or sorrow for sin, and to seek God's favor.
A grain that grows like grass and was baked into bread, mostly eaten by poorer people. It was also food for horses, and its harvest came in spring, before the wheat harvest.
To admit that you did something wrong, such as a sin or a fault, by owning up to it and saying it openly.
To say openly that you believe in a person or a thing, or to declare that something is true instead of denying it.
To openly acknowledge someone as one's own, like a true follower, friend, or child. In Matthew 10:32, Jesus says He will do this for people before His Father.
A strong, fortified place, like a fort or fortress, where people can be safe.
A place where things are stored and kept safe, such as grain or other supplies. It can also describe a source full of valuable things, like wisdom and knowledge.
Cherubim are winged beings, not angels, who stay close to God and look like mixes of different animals. In the Bible they guard Eden, hold up God's throne, and show that He is present.
A Roman army officer in charge of about a hundred soldiers. He was a captain of a group called a century.
A shekel was an ancient Hebrew unit of weight, about 0.4 ounces. People weighed out silver, gold and other things in shekels, and shekels were also used as money.
Hail is frozen rain that falls from the sky as hard lumps of ice, usually during a thunderstorm. In the Bible, God sometimes uses it to bring judgment, as in the plague on Egypt.
A greeting that wishes someone well, like saying "Greetings!" In Matthew, the soldiers use it to mock Jesus, pretending to honor Him as king.
Something hidden that God uncovers and makes known to people, or the act of making it known. God shows His truth and plans, and the Bible is this truth written down.
Affliction is a hard thing that causes lasting pain or sorrow in body or mind, like sickness, loss, or being mistreated. It can also mean the state of suffering that comes from such troubles.
A cloth covering, often thin, worn on the head or over the face. It could be a pretty part of a woman's dress, or worn by a bride-to-be meeting her future husband.
A curtain hung up to block the view and hide something from sight. In the Bible's tabernacle and temple, a veil of this kind hung in the sacred place of worship.
Something that covers, disguises or hides, like a mask or pretense. It can describe something that keeps a thing hidden, as when understanding is covered over.
The Hittites were an ancient people descended from Heth, a son of Canaan. They lived in the land of Canaan, near Hebron, and were strong enough to fight against Israel.
A transgression is breaking a law or command, like going past a line that was set. It is a wrong act or sin against what is right.
To cut off the foreskin of a boy or man. This was a religious sign for God's people, and "the circumcised" can mean the Jewish people.
To change the heart, not the body. It means to turn away from stubbornness and be willing to obey God.
A woman who has never had sex. In the Bible, it is often a young woman, and sometimes one promised in marriage.
A title the prophets use for a whole people or city, such as Israel or Sidon, as if it were a young woman.
A tablet is a flat piece of material, such as stone, used for writing, painting, drawing, or carving on. It can also hold words written or carved on it.
An ordinance is a rule set up by someone with authority. In the Bible it is usually a law or command from God, and sometimes a set way of doing a ceremony.
To glorify is to praise and honor someone or something, showing how great or excellent it is. It can also mean to make someone glorious, lifting them up to great honor.
Faithfulness is being loyal and keeping your promises. It means sticking to your duty and to the people you love, and always being true to your word.
Money or valuable things paid to a ruler to show submission, win peace and protection, or give honor. It can also mean a tax paid to a king.
The Amalekites were a tribe who moved from place to place with their flocks in the deserts south of Canaan. They attacked Israel several times, and Saul and David later broke their power.
A talent was a very heavy weight used for measuring gold and silver. It was also the name for that amount of money, so talents were used for very large sums.
Caesar was the title of the Roman emperor, who ruled Judea. Roman citizens paid taxes to him and could ask him to hear their court case.
A religious ceremony using water, as a sign of being cleansed from sin. John the Baptist used it, and Christ's followers continued it.
The sufferings of Christ. Jesus uses the word for the hard things He would go through.
Having all power, with no limit to His strength. Almighty is a name for God, the all-powerful One.
Something detestable is extremely hateful and disgusting. It deserves to be strongly hated and rejected.
To afflict is to cause someone pain or deep trouble, in the body or in the mind. Someone who is afflicted is suffering grief or distress that keeps going or comes again and again.
A serpent is a snake, and some kinds are poisonous. In the Bible, the word can also stand for a sly, harmful enemy, and Satan is called the old serpent.
A Greek is a person from Greece. In the New Testament the word can also mean any non-Jewish person, and Greek is the language of Greece.
The people of Rome, the great city that ruled the lands around it. In these verses, Romans are the people who held power over the nation or who held the rights of Roman citizens.
Vengeance is punishment given in return for a wrong. When it is about God, it means His fair punishment of wrongdoers, describing what He does, not how He feels.
A banquet is a big, fancy feast given for a group of invited guests. The master of the house, or a leader chosen for the day, was in charge.
Blameless means free from blame, with no fault that people could rightly point to. A blameless person is innocent and does not deserve to be scolded or accused.
Lasting forever with no end. For God it means He has always been and always will be, and it also describes promises, kingdoms, and joy that never stop.
The rising of the dead back to life. The Bible teaches this about Jesus, who rose from the dead, and about all people who will rise again at the end.
The state of being risen from the dead, or the life after people are raised. "In the resurrection" means in that future time when the dead have risen.
A group of Jewish religious leaders in Jesus' time, many of them priests of high position. They did not believe the dead rise again, or that angels exist, and they accepted only Moses' written law.
Unleavened bread is bread made without leaven, which is something like yeast that makes dough rise. It has not been raised by leaven.
A big, strong tree that can live a very long time. The Hebrew word means "strong," and some verses may mean a similar tree, like a terebinth.
To make a person or thing clean in the way God's law asked, removing whatever made them unclean, so they were fit for worship and sacred work.
To free a person or people from guilt and the stain of sin, making their hearts clean.
To make something clear and clean by removing anything mixed in that does not belong, like dirt in metal.
A cubit was an old way to measure length, based on the distance from a person's elbow to the tip of the middle finger. It is about 18 inches, or 45.7 centimeters.
A savior is someone who saves people and keeps them safe from danger or ruin. In the Bible, Jesus Christ is the Savior who opens the way to everlasting life.
To make a heart stubborn, proud, or unwilling to listen or change. In the Bible, a person can harden his own heart, and God can also harden a heart.
To sow is to scatter seed over the ground so that it can grow into plants. The word can also mean to spread something around.
To prove or show that someone or something is right, or to defend it as right. Cards 1 and 2 use it this way, as someone trying to make himself look right or not guilty.
When God justifies people, He forgives their sins and accepts them as right with Him because they believe in Christ. It is a gift of His grace, not something they earn.
An Edomite is someone from Esau's family line. Esau was the brother of Jacob, and his people lived in the land of Edom.
Upset and uneasy because someone else has, or might get, the love, honor, or good things you want. This is how people feel toward a rival.
When said about God, it means He wants His people's whole love and worship and will not share it with any rival. It can also mean He cares deeply and protects what is His.
Rebellion is refusing to obey the people in charge, or fighting against them. In the Bible, it can mean turning against God, and it can also mean wrongdoing or sin.
Breaking a marriage promise by having a sexual relationship with someone who is not your husband or wife. God's commands treat it as a serious sin and a great wrong.
Being unfaithful to God. The Bible pictures God's bond with His people like a marriage, so turning away to idols or false gods is called adultery.
Wrong, impure thinking as well as wrong actions. Jesus teaches that looking at someone with lust is adultery in the heart.
Our Lord recognized adultery as the only ground for divorce. Jesus teaches that divorcing a spouse for other reasons and marrying someone else is adultery.
A tithe is a tenth of what the land and animals produce, set apart and given to God. In Israel it supported the Levites and the worship of God.
A maidservant is a girl or woman who works as a servant.
To persecute is to treat someone cruelly and unfairly again and again, to hurt and trouble them. It often means doing this to people because of what they believe or how they worship.
A place that has been destroyed and left empty, with no people living there. It can also mean the act of wiping out a place, or the lasting state of being ruined and deserted.
A Samaritan was someone from Samaria. In Jesus' time it meant a people descended from settlers Assyria's king brought there, and the Jews and Samaritans were bitter enemies.
Spiritual describes what is not physical, or what has to do with the spirit or soul. It often means guided by God's Spirit, the opposite of what is only earthly.
A sweet-smelling substance, or its pleasant smell. People used perfumes on their bodies, clothes, and beds, in worship, and to prepare the dead for burial.
Fatherless describes a child whose father has died, so the child has no living father.
A very hot, closed-in place where a fire burns. People used furnaces to melt and clean metals like silver and gold, to burn limestone, and to bake clay.
A picture for a place or time of great suffering and hard testing, like the hard slavery in Egypt or the trials God uses to test His people.
A huge furnace used to punish people. King Nebuchadnezzar's was shaped like a big oven for baking bricks, with one opening high up for loading and another low down for taking things out.
Refusing to obey or resisting someone who has the right to be in charge. In the Bible, rebellious people turn away from God and will not obey Him.
A steward is someone trusted to manage a household, property, or the people and food in his care for another person. In the New Testament, ministers and Christians are called God's stewards.
An Asherah was a wooden pole or image used to worship a false goddess of the Canaanites, and the word can also mean the goddess herself. God's people were told to cut these poles down.
A special piece of priest's clothing with a front and back part, joined at the shoulders and fastened at the waist. The high priest's was embroidered in bright colors.
Something like the priest's ephod that was made and kept for worship, such as in a shrine. Schaff's says other people besides priests also wore an ephod or something like it.
The Gibeonites were the people who lived in Gibeon.
A Midianite was a person from the Midianites, a tribe named after a man called Midian and descended from him. They were wandering herders and traders who lived in tents in the Arabian desert.
A palm is a tree of warm lands, often tall, with a plain trunk and a crown of big leaves at the top. Its branches were also a sign of victory.
The palm is the inner part of the hand, between the wrist and the fingers.
A concubine was a woman married to a man, but with a lower status than a wife. She had no say in running the family, though her children belonged to it.
The Benjamites were the people of the tribe of Benjamin. They came from Benjamin's family and lived after him, and together they made up one of the tribes of Israel.
A man who has just gotten married, or a man who is about to be married.
A redeemer is a family member whose duty is to set things right for a relative, winning back what was lost and defending against wrongs. God is called Redeemer of His people.
A Reubenite is someone from the family of Reuben who lived after him. The Reubenites were the people of the tribe of Reuben, one of Israel's tribes.
Being pure and good in a way that is set apart for God. God is perfectly holy, while people who follow Him grow in holiness little by little.
A painful worry about losing someone's love or loyalty, like a husband who suspects his wife is unfaithful. For God, it is His strong concern that His people stay faithful to Him.
An uneasy, bitter feeling toward others because they have honor, success, or advantages that you want for yourself.
A fierce, burning passion, like the strong feeling of love that does not give up.
A word that means "true" or "so be it." People say it to agree with what was said, to promise it is true, or to end a prayer.
Dew is water that gathers in tiny drops on the ground and plants during the night. In Palestine it watered the land when there was no rain, so it was a sign of blessing.
A lump of old dough mixed into fresh dough to make bread rise and turn light. God's people could not use it during Passover or in offerings burned to Him.
A picture of something that spreads secretly through a whole group. It can mean bad teaching or evil, like the Pharisees', or how God's kingdom quietly grows.
Speaking as a prophet. This can mean telling what will happen in the future, or teaching and explaining religious things, such as preaching to people.
Reproach is shame or insulting words aimed at someone. To reproach someone is to blame them harshly or make fun of them.
To pierce is to push into or through something with a pointed object, like a spear, arrow, or awl. It can also mean to hurt someone deeply, as pain or sadness does.
The food God miraculously gave the Israelites each day in the wilderness. It was small and round, tasted like honey wafers, and its name is like a question meaning "What is it?"
The Sanhedrin was the top group of Jewish leaders who met together to make decisions, especially about religious matters. Its name comes from a Greek word for "council."
A seer was a prophet, a person who received visions from God. In early Israel people used this name for the one they went to when they wanted to ask God something.
A citadel is a strong fortress inside or near a city. It protected the city and was the last place to defend if enemies attacked.
Cutting off the foreskin, the skin covering the tip of the penis. God gave this as a sign of His promise to Abraham's family, done to boys at eight days old.
A name for the Jewish people, who were circumcised, as opposed to the Gentiles, called "the uncircumcision." Some cards use it for a group who held to this practice.
A picture of a clean heart, changed inside by God's Spirit, and not only a mark on the body. It means turning away from sin.
In Philippians, the name for people whose hearts are made clean by God's Spirit, those who truly belong to Him, whether or not they are marked on the body.
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. He led the capture of Jerusalem and, as the king commanded, treated the prophet Jeremiah kindly.
Repentance is feeling truly sorry for sin and turning away from it toward God. It is a change of mind and purpose that leads to a new way of living.
A tunic was a long, loose piece of clothing worn in ancient times, sometimes with sleeves. People often wore it under other clothes, and a belt held it at the waist.
A musical instrument with strings, a kind of harp. People in ancient times used it a lot, often to play along with poetry.
The first crops and goods gathered in a season, like grain, new wine, oil, and wool. God's people gave this first part to Him, through the priests, to thank Him.
The first and earliest result of something. Christ is called the firstfruits because He was raised from the dead first, before those who belong to Him.
Thanksgiving is saying thank you to God for the good things and kindness He has given. It can also mean a public celebration of God's goodness.
A staff that a ruler or leader holds as a sign of his power to rule. The word can also stand for that royal power itself.
A person who is skilled in magic and practices it. The word can also mean someone who explains signs and uncovers secret things.
A teaching or custom handed down from one person or group to another, often by word of mouth instead of in writing. Some traditions were good, but others people used to push aside God's commands.
To treat something holy with disrespect or make it unclean, like God's name, His Sabbaths or His sanctuary. As a describing word, it means not holy or disrespectful toward holy things.
The Jebusites were one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel came, and their city Jebus was Jerusalem. They were not fully driven out until King David captured it.
Precepts are rules or commands about how to act, especially how to do what is right. In these verses, they are God's commands.
Slavery is being a slave, completely under another person's control and made to work for him. A slave is not free to make his own choices.
Slavery can also mean being held under the power of something other than a person, like sin or fear, so that you are not free to act or choose as you wish.
An oppressor is someone who treats others cruelly and unfairly. He puts heavy burdens on people and is harsh with them, and he may use unfair laws.
To make someone or something holy by setting it apart for God's use. It can also mean to cleanse a person from sin and make them pure.
When God sanctifies Himself, He protects His honor from the insults of wicked people and shows His glory as a holy God.
A shout that means "Praise the LORD!" It is used in songs of praise and thanks to God, and it became a common way to praise Him.
Melchizedek was the king of Salem and a priest of God Most High. He blessed Abram and received a tenth from him, and the Bible later compares Jesus, a priest forever, to him.
The priesthood is the job of being a priest, a person set apart for holy work. It also means the whole group of men who serve as priests.
A cupbearer was an important servant who worked for a king. His job was to fill the king's cup and hand it to him personally.
The Baals were false gods worshiped by the Canaanites and nearby peoples. Baal means "lord," and each place had its own Baal, seen as a chief male god.
A census is an official counting of the people in a land. Leaders wrote down how many people there were, often to collect money or to see how many men could serve in an army.
Cephas is another name for Peter. It comes from a Syriac word meaning "rock," and Jesus gave this name to Simon.
The light, dry outer coverings of wheat seeds, blown away by the wind when grain was tossed into the air. In the Bible, it pictures wicked people and worthless things.
Zeal is strong, eager feeling for a person or cause. It can be good or bad, and the Bible says God has it too, as when He cares deeply and acts.
Anointing means putting or pouring oil on a person or thing to set it apart as holy. In the Bible, priests, kings, and sacred objects were anointed for God's special use.
Anointing can also be spiritual, not done with oil but with the Holy Spirit. The Bible says Jesus, God's promised Deliverer (the Messiah), was anointed with the Holy Spirit in this way.
The people of Assyria, or the ones who lived there. In the Bible, the Assyrians are the people of that land.
Oholibah is the name of a sister in Ezekiel's picture story, and her name may mean a tent is in her. She stands for Jerusalem, shown as an unfaithful wife.
To ordain is to appoint or set someone apart for a special job or office. It also means to decide or command that something be done, as when God sets something in place.
A diviner is someone who claims to tell what will happen, or to reveal hidden things, by using supernatural powers.
A place where grapes were squeezed to get their juice. It usually had two large basins cut in rock: grapes were stomped in the upper one, and the juice flowed down into the lower one.
To dedicate something is to set it apart for a special purpose, often in a solemn ceremony. Most often it means giving a person, a building, or treasures to God.
A person who watches over other people or their work and makes sure things are done well. He is a supervisor, like a boss, who is put in charge.
A leader who cares for a church, also called a pastor or elder. He watches over the group of Christians and guides them.
A small metal container used by priests to carry burning coals from the altar. They sprinkled incense on the coals, and the sweet-smelling smoke filled the place of worship.
A small, shallow drum with one skin that is played by hitting it with the hand. It has little bells on its sides, so it jingles when played.
A sacred place or object, such as an altar, or a case or box where holy things are kept. It is a place set apart as holy.
A trespass is a sin: doing something wrong against someone, or breaking a rule about what you know you should do. In the Bible, it is especially breaking God's law or command.
Forgiveness is when someone who did wrong is pardoned and treated as not guilty. It also means being ready and willing to forgive, as God is toward sins.
Perverse means turned away from what is right. A perverse person stubbornly does wrong and goes against what is good, even when told not to.
Not circumcised. The word is also used for someone who is not one of the Israelites, like the Philistine Goliath whom David calls "this uncircumcised Philistine."
The Kohathites were the family of Levites who came from Kohath. They camped south of the tabernacle and carried its most holy objects, like the ark, on their shoulders.
A person who lived in Ephesus, a famous city in Asia Minor. Paul also wrote a letter to the Christians there, called Ephesians.
A large black bird of the crow family that eats mostly dead animals and flies far to find food. God did not allow ravens as food, and He cares for them.
A leper is a person who has leprosy, a terrible skin disease. In the Bible, people with this disease were kept apart from others.
A sweet-smelling gum from the sap of a small thorny tree. It was used in perfume, holy anointing oil, and for preparing the dead, and it was given as a valuable gift.
A sweet-smelling resin, probably from the rockrose shrub, though no one is sure. It was carried by traders and sent as a gift.
A Nazirite is someone who is set apart. The word means "one separated" or "one consecrated," which means a person who is made special and kept apart for a purpose.
A ransom is a price paid to buy someone's freedom or save a life, or something given in someone's place. The Bible says Christ gave His life as a ransom for many.
A worshiper is someone who worships. This person honors and adores a being or thing as holy, like God, or in some verses, an idol.
Oppression is cruel and unfair treatment by people with power, who put heavy burdens on others. It brings hardship, misery, and suffering to those who are treated this way.
A musical instrument made of two round metal plates that were clashed together to make a loud, ringing sound. Cymbals were played in worship, in the temple, and at celebrations.
Dominion is the power and right to rule and control. It can also mean the land or people a ruler governs, and God's dominion is everlasting.
A turban is a head covering made of a cap with a long strip of cloth, often fine linen, wound around it.
A eunuch was a man who could not have children, either from birth or because he was made that way. Many served kings as officials, guards, or attendants.
A deep hole or tank, often cut into rock, that holds rain water for later use. Springs were scarce in Palestine, and empty cisterns were sometimes used as prisons.
A poisonous snake whose bite can kill. In the Bible, a viper can also stand for something deceitful and harmful, like a dangerous person.
Persecution is treating people cruelly and unjustly, by causing them pain, loss, or even death, because of what they believe or how they worship. God's people have suffered it in every age.
A round red fruit about the size of an orange, with a hard skin and juicy, seed-filled pulp. Decorations shaped like it were on the high priest's robe and the temple pillars.
A sweet-smelling, sticky substance from a tree that hardens into bits, brought from Arabia. It was burned for its fragrance, mixed into the holy incense, and added to offerings in God's worship.
Freewill describes something given or done by choice, because a person wants to and not because anyone forces them. It means the action is voluntary and comes freely from the person.
In the Bible, leprosy was a name for several skin diseases, often with white scaly patches and sores. Sick people had to live apart from others.
The magi were wise men of the East, a group of priests and scholars. They studied the stars and advised kings, and they were also thought to tell the future and explain dreams.
A wild animal of Africa and Asia that is related to dogs and wolves. Jackals hunt at night, eat dead animals, and are known for their loud, sad howling.
Acacia is a twisted, thorny tree that grows in the Sinai desert. Its wood is called shittim wood in the Bible, and the Israelites used it to build the tabernacle and its furniture.
A Mede was a person from Media, a land in Asia. The Medes were a people the Bible names as living in that land.
A simple hut made from tree branches or other light materials, used for a short stay. The Israelites lived in booths at the feast of Tabernacles to remember the wilderness.
A small stall or stand where a person sits to do work. In the Gospels, it is the place where Matthew and Levi sat to collect taxes.
An adversary is someone who stands against you, like an enemy or a foe. It can be a fighter against you, or someone on the other side in a court case.
Deliverance is being rescued or set free from danger, trouble, or captivity. It is the act of saving someone from something that threatens or holds them.
A huge, scary sea creature whose name means "twisted" or "coiled." It may be a crocodile, a whale, or a great serpent, and it can also stand for an enemy.
Perseverance is sticking with something and not giving up, even when it is hard. It means you keep going steadily instead of quitting.
A covered porch at the entrance of a building, often with a row of pillars. In the Bible, it is the entrance porch at the front of the temple or of a temple gate.
A signet is a seal, often worn as a ring, that a king used to mark his documents as truly his. It could also seal other things.
A doorpost is the upright post at the side of a doorway. God told the Jews to write His words on the doorposts of their houses.
To punish someone who has done wrong, in order to make things right for the one who was hurt. When God avenges, He upholds His own law and punishes those who do evil.
An avenger is someone who avenges, standing up for what is right or taking vengeance for a wrong. The Bible phrase "avenger of blood" uses this word.
The elect are the people God has chosen to save. They are close to Him and live holy lives.
Fellowship is a close, friendly sharing between people, or between people and God. It means being together as friends and having something in common.
A footstool is a low stool that holds up your feet while you sit. In the Bible, God's footstool is the ark, where His glory rested above it between the cherubim, or the whole earth.
Making enemies a footstool means bringing them fully under someone's power, so they are completely defeated and ruled.
Living in a way that honors God. It comes from knowing and loving Him, and it shows in respect for Him and in glad, steady obedience to what He commands.
In the phrase "the mystery of godliness," the word means the heart of the faith God has revealed to people, the core of what believers hold to be true.
Redemption is buying back something that was lost, or rescuing someone from trouble or bondage, often by paying a price. In the Bible, Christ's blood frees His people from sin.
The threshold is the piece of wood or stone that lies under a door. You step over it when you go through the entrance of a house, temple, or gate.
Unblemished means having no flaw, stain, or fault. The sources also say it can mean free from deformity, so it describes something that is perfect, with nothing wrong with it.
Showing great honor and respect to someone or something. Worship is right when it is given to God, but it is idolatry when given to idols or false gods.
An adulteress is a woman who commits adultery, breaking a marriage promise. The Bible can also use the word for someone who breaks her promises to God.
A brier is a prickly, thorny plant or shrub. In the Bible, briers often grow wild where land is not cared for, and they can stand for something painful or troublesome.
Impurity is being unclean or dirty. It can mean being unclean in a religious way, or it can mean anything bad or mixed in that spoils something.
To win someone over to your idea or choice by giving reasons, advice, or pleading. To be persuaded is to be convinced or led to believe or do something.
A torrent is a fast, violent rush of water, like a stream that suddenly swells and pours down a steep place. It can also mean any strong, rushing flow.
A drunkard is a person who often drinks too much of alcoholic drinks, such as wine, and gets drunk. It is a habit for that person, not just one time.
Selah is a word in the Psalms that was probably a music term. No one knows for sure what it meant, but it may have marked a pause or quiet break.
An important stone at the corner of a building that joins two walls together. The Bible also uses it for an important leader, and it is used for Jesus.
To fan something is to stir the air so a fire burns stronger. A fan is also a tool that tosses grain into the wind so the chaff blows away.
To fan a flame can also mean to make something stronger, the way stirring the air makes a fire burn higher. In 2 Timothy 1:6, it means to strengthen God's gift.
A powerful feeling or desire that takes hold of a person and can be hard to control, such as anger, love, or eager wanting. In these verses, such feelings often lead people toward wrong things.
Sorcery is magic that people claimed to do with the help of evil spirits, like telling the future or healing sickness. The Bible warns of very serious punishment for it.
A petition is a serious, formal request for something needed or wanted, made to God or to a king or other leader. To petition is to make that request.
To pardon is to forgive someone for doing wrong. When God pardons, He forgives sin freely and removes it from the person.
A very deep opening with no bottom, so deep that it seems to go on forever. The word is also used for a deep place and for hell.
The name of a month on the Jewish calendar. It is the last of the twelve months and comes around late winter, in February and March.
A tribe of people who lived in Canaan, descended from Canaan the son of Ham. Many lived in the north near Mount Hermon and Lebanon, and some also lived in Gibeon.
A special year that came every fiftieth year for the Israelites. Hebrew slaves were set free, land went back to its first family, and trumpets announced it.
Belonging to the Levites, who came from Levi. It can also mean priestly.
Obedience is doing what someone in authority tells you to do, or staying away from what they forbid. It means following a command you know about, whether you choose to or are made to.
Describes someone who does not honor God or obey Him. An ungodly person is wicked and sinful, and ignores God's commands.
A wrong thing someone does, such as a crime, a sin, or an injury to another person.
Something that causes people to trip up in their faith or fall into sin. It can also be someone or something people strongly disapprove of.
To "take offense" is to feel displeased or angry at someone because of what he is or does.
A dry measure used for grain and flour, about 20 dry quarts or 22 liters. An omer was a tenth of an ephah.
The name of a son of Midian, and of a city named after him. The city was in Midian, a land with many camels.
Divination is trying to learn secret things or the future by using signs like arrows, cups, or dreams, not God. God's law forbade it, and the word can also mean false predictions.
A hypocrite is someone who pretends to be better or more godly than he really is. He acts good or religious on the outside, often to win praise from others.
A mina was an amount of weight and money. In Ezekiel it was 60 shekels, about 1.5 pounds, while in Jesus' parable it was most likely a silver coin worth about a hundred days' wages.
Following the special rules and ceremonies people were to keep. Someone who is ceremonially unclean is unclean by those rules.
Fasts are special times when people go without food to show sadness, humility, and that they depend on God. Judah kept set fast days each year, and God says these will become joyful feasts.
Godless describes someone who does not honor or respect God. Such a person lives in a wicked way, as if God did not matter.
Perishing means dying or being destroyed, or being completely lost. It can be about losing one's life, such as from hunger or drowning, or about being lost forever.
A porch is a covered entrance to a building, like a small room or hallway at the front. Some were big enough to work as a covered walkway.
Having to do with a priest or the work of priests. It can also mean fitting for a priest.
To be stoned means to be pelted with stones. Someone who is stoned has stones thrown at him or her.
A tall tower where a guard stands to watch for enemies or any danger coming near.
Admitting your sins to God and saying you were wrong, as Joshua told Achan to do. It can also mean owning up to a wrong done to another person.
A statement of what a person believes about God and His Son, as when Timothy and Jesus made the good confession. It can also be a belief that believers share, as in "common confession."
A deliverer is someone who rescues people and keeps them safe. In the book of Judges, the Lord raised up a deliverer for Israel.
A small woods or group of trees growing together. In the Bible, this is often a planted orchard, like olive trees.
A group of trees set apart for worshiping false gods. People put idols there, and God's people were forbidden to worship in such places.
To defend someone or something against blame or attack and stand up for what is right. When God vindicates people, He defends them and upholds their rights, bringing justice to those who are in need.
Raisins are grapes that have been dried, either in the sun or by heat. In the Bible they are a food people carried, ate, and shared.
Ascents are ways of going up, like climbing a hill or rising to a high place. In "a song of ascents," the word is part of the song's label.
Ordination is the act of setting someone apart for a special job or office in God's service. It means a person is appointed and given holy duties.
A people who lived in the land of Canaan before Israel came. The name means "villagers," and they seem to have lived out in the open country, while the Canaanites lived in the cities.
A tool for cutting crops at harvest time. It has a curved blade like a hook, and people swung it to cut grain or gather other ripe crops, like grapes.
Having strong feelings and eagerness for someone or something. A zealous person is ardent and fully committed to what they care about.
To gather the grain or fruit that harvesters leave behind in a field or vineyard. God's law told farmers to leave some for the poor to pick up.
A child who has lost a father or mother, or both. The Bible tells God's people to treat orphans kindly and to care for them.
In John 14:18, people left alone with no one to care for or protect them, as if they had no parent.
A tall evergreen tree with hard, sweet-smelling wood that lasts a very long time. Experts are not sure which tree the Bible means; it may be a juniper, pine, or fir.
A physician is a doctor, a person trained in the art of healing who treats sick or hurt people and gives them remedies to help them get well.
Someone who heals people's inner, moral troubles, the way a doctor heals the body. In Job, the word is used this way for people who fail at it.
An unbeliever is a person who does not believe, especially someone who does not accept the Bible as God's message or does not accept Christ's teachings or who He is.
To flog someone is to hit them again and again with a whip or rod, usually as a punishment.
To reconcile is to end a quarrel or settle a disagreement so there is peace. When it is about God, it means people, and even all things, being brought to peace with Him through Jesus.
A sorcerer is a magician or enchanter, someone who claimed to have power with evil spirits. The Bible says sorcery brings very severe punishment.
A prickly weed with sharp points that grows in fields and wild places. It is a troublesome plant that farmers do not want growing among their crops.
To speak about God or something holy with terrible disrespect, insulting it or talking badly about it. It can also mean to speak evil of someone or something that people honor.
To claim for oneself the rights or powers that belong only to God, such as the power to forgive sins.
To keep going with something you have started, and not give up, even when it is hard or when people or troubles try to stop you.
The special rights and honor that belonged to the oldest son in a family. These could include a double share of the property, the father's blessing, and leading the family.
A manslayer is a person who killed someone by accident, not on purpose and not out of hatred. He was allowed to run to a city of refuge to be safe.
An oracle is a message that comes from God, or is said to come from a god. A prophet may speak it, often to tell what God wants or what will happen.
The Rechabites were a family descended from Jonadab, son of Rechab. He told them never to drink wine or own houses or land, so they lived in tents and obeyed him faithfully.
A satrap was an official who governed a province for a king. The word is mainly linked to ancient Persia, and the Bible also uses it for officials of other kings.
People who make fun of others and look down on them. In the last days, such people will follow their own desires and ask, "Where is the promise of His coming?"
Sheaves are bundles of grain stalks, such as wheat, rye, or barley, tied together after being cut.
A sling is a weapon made of a strap and two strings. A stone is whirled around in it and sent flying when one string is let go, and to sling also means to throw.
Tribulation is great trouble and suffering, like the hard times that come when people are mistreated for following God's word. Jesus said His followers would face it in the world.
Blasphemy is speaking evil or insulting words against God, showing Him disrespect. The word can also mean cruel, abusive talk against people or things, but in the Bible it mostly means insulting God.
Gleanings are the bits of crops left in the field, on the vines, or on the trees after the harvesters finish; gleaning is gathering them. God's law told Israel to leave them for the poor.
A person from Galilee, the northern part of the land of Israel. Jesus and many of His apostles were Galileans, and people from Galilee were known for the way they talked.
Baptizing means giving someone the sacrament of baptism, a sacred act done in the Church. In older English the word could also mean to name someone or to make something holy.
Dedication is the act of setting something apart for a special purpose, often with a solemn ceremony. It can mean giving something to God or to a holy use, like a temple.
The Feast of Dedication is another name for Hanukkah, a celebration of the temple being rededicated after the Maccabean Revolt.
A Roman silver coin. One denarius was the usual pay for a day of work, so it was about what a laborer earned in a day.
Fasted means went without food for a time on purpose. People in the Bible did this as a religious act, often to show sadness, grief, or that they were sorry.
A lawgiver is someone who makes or creates laws for people to follow. It is another word for a person who writes or passes laws.
Lawlessness is living without being held back by law, which leads to disorder. In the Bible it means breaking God's Law, and it is what sin is.
A medium is a person who claims to be a go-between for spirits or the dead, passing along their messages. God warns His people not to go to them.
Onyx is a valuable stone with bands of different colors. Its gems were set in the high priest's special clothing, and it came from a land called Havilah.
A prophetess is a woman who is a prophet. She may tell what will happen in the future, like Miriam, Huldah, and Anna.
Purification was a special religious cleansing under God's law. It made an unclean person clean again so they could worship with God's people, usually using water, washing, and often sacrifices.
Purification can also mean being cleansed from sin and its guilt, not only from the kind of uncleanness the law talked about.
The Sidonians were the people who lived in the city of Sidon.
Scattering a liquid, like water or blood, in small drops. In the Bible, the high priest sprinkled blood in the holy place to make things right for the people's sin.
Not believing or trusting what God has said, or refusing to trust Jesus and the good news about Him. It can also mean doubting God's promises and faithfulness.
Weak faith, where a person truly believes but still has doubts. The father in Mark 9:24 trusts Jesus, yet he asks for help with his doubting.
To offend someone is to displease them, upset them, or hurt their feelings. It can also mean to do wrong or break God's law, which is to sin.
A time of feasting or celebration, often on a day of joy. It could be a religious day or an ordinary one.
A very large bird from Africa and Arabia with a long neck and short wings, so it cannot fly. It likes lonely, empty places and has a sad, piercing cry.
A genealogy is a record of a person's or family's ancestors and children, listed in order from one generation to the next. The Hebrews thought these lists were very important.
A small bird that eats seeds and is common in the Holy Land. Sparrows were sold for almost nothing, and Jesus used them to show how much God cares for His people.
Put to death by being hung up by the neck. This was a way of carrying out a punishment.
Hung up or fastened to a high place, with nothing holding it up from below. Here it is used for bodies that were already dead.
Idolatry is worshiping idols, meaning statues or anything people make or put in God's place. The people of Israel kept falling into it again and again, even though God had warned them.
A kinsman is a man who belongs to the same family or race as you, someone related to you by blood. In Israel, the nearest male relative had special duties to help his family.
A name for a sister in Ezekiel's story. It may mean "her own tent" or "worship place," and it stands for Samaria, pictured as an unfaithful wife who turned to Assyria.
Rabbi means "my master." It was a respectful title the Jews gave to teachers of God's Law, and people often used it when speaking to Jesus.

Being ceremonially unclean, which cut a person off for a time from the privileges of living among God's people. It came from ordinary things like body sicknesses, and it was a ritual kind of uncleanness.
The dirty, sinful state of a person who has done wrong. It is moral impurity that makes someone unfit before God and in need of being cleansed or saved by Him.
To graft is to join a small shoot or branch to a tree so the two grow together as one. In Romans 11, it pictures believers being joined to God's people.
The Kenites were a tribe living in the desert between southern Canaan and Mount Sinai. Moses' father-in-law Jethro was one of them, and they were kind and friendly to Israel.
A deacon is a servant and helper in the church. Deacons help take care of practical jobs, like giving to the poor, so the church leaders can focus on teaching and prayer.
An owl is a bird that is mostly active at night and has large eyes. The Bible names several kinds, often living in ruins, so owls came to stand for empty, wrecked places.
A pearl is a smooth, shiny gem, usually round, that forms inside the shell of an oyster. People in Bible times treasured pearls as some of the most valuable gems and wore them as jewelry.
A small, dangerous creature, related to spiders, that lives in hot, dry places. It has claws and a curved stinger at the end of its tail that gives a very painful sting.
In 1 Kings 12:11, a harsh kind of whip, perhaps with knots or stones that gave a stinging pain. It may also be just a figure of speech for a very cruel punishment.
Wicked or hostile people, spoken of as if they were scorpions. In Ezekiel 2:6 it pictures dangerous people who could hurt someone.
A cherub is a winged being that belongs near God, and cherubim means more than one. Cherubs guarded Eden, were shown on the lid of the ark, and carry God's throne.
Cleansing is the act of making someone or something clean. In the Bible it means being freed from dirt, guilt, or anything that made a person unfit to worship, and made pure.
A hailstone is a lump of ice that falls from a cloud. It is like a raindrop that has frozen solid.
A woman who is paid to have sex. In Bible times, people looked down on harlots, and the Law and Proverbs warn against them.
A wicked city or nation, such as Jerusalem, Israel, or Nineveh. Israel became a harlot by worshiping idols, like breaking a marriage promise to God.
Hyssop was a plant with a stem that grew on walls. It was used for sprinkling and in cleansing ceremonies, though no one is sure exactly which plant it was.
Willing to do what someone in charge says. An obedient person follows commands and teachings, doing what is required and staying away from what is forbidden.

Obeying means doing what someone in charge tells you to do, yielding to their authority and following their commands. It can also mean submitting to something, like the truth, and following what it teaches.
Partiality is favoring one person or side over another without a fair reason. It can lead to unfair judgments, because a person's mind leans one way instead of weighing what is true and right.
A bundle of cut grain stalks, such as wheat or barley, tied together.
A betrayer is someone who turns against a person who trusted them. Another word for this kind of person is a traitor.
A Gittite is a person from Gath, a city of the Philistines. Obed-edom is called one, and so are the 600 men who came with David from Gath.
The Merarites were a Levite family who came from a man named Merari. They carried the heavy parts of the tabernacle, like the boards, bars and pillars.
A Simeonite is a person from the tribe of Simeon, one of the tribes of Israel. The word can also describe a family or group that belongs to that tribe.
A fugitive is someone who runs away or escapes from danger, enemies, or punishment. It can also mean a wanderer with no settled home.
A deceiver is someone who tricks others and leads them into believing something false. He may be a cheat or a fake who pretends to be something he is not.
A kind of dove with a sad, cooing call that comes to Palestine in early spring. Poor people could bring turtledoves as sacrifices when they could not afford a lamb.
A wafer is a thin cake. In the Bible, wafers were used in various offerings to God.
Beelzebul means "lord of the house." It was the name of a false god, and the Jews thought he ruled the evil spirits, the same as Satan.
Denarii is the plural of denarius, a coin that was usually a laborer's pay for one day of work.
A Jewish political group who supported King Herod's family and agreed that the Jews should obey Rome. They joined the Pharisees against Jesus.

A mediator is someone who stands between two sides and helps them, either by settling their quarrel or by carrying messages between them, as Moses did. Christ is the one mediator between God and people.
A paralytic is a person who has paralysis, also called palsy. That means the person has lost the power to move parts of the body.
A small bird, related to the partridge, that people hunt for food. In these verses, God sent huge flocks of quail to the Israelites to eat.
Offering something to God as an act of worship, such as an animal laid on an altar. People sacrificed to say thank you, to ask for His favor, or to make up for sin.
Stocks were a wooden tool for punishing prisoners by holding their feet fast between two beams. Some kinds also held the neck and arms, so the body was bent over.
Having strings. A stringed instrument is a musical instrument that makes its sound with strings.
A very bitter plant. In the Bible it stands for bitterness, sorrow, and hard suffering, and being made to eat or drink it shows great pain.
In Revelation, the name of a star that falls on the waters and turns a third of them bitter. The name comes from the bitter plant.
A man who has sex with a woman who is married to someone else. The Bible also uses the word for people who break their promise to God.
A dungeon is a prison that is harsher than an ordinary one. It was a dark, closed-in place, like a deep cell or pit, where people were locked up as punishment.
A person from Ethiopia, a land probably in the upper Nile region. In the Hebrew Bible the word is "Cushite," and it is used for people like Zerah and Ebed-melech.
What a teacher teaches as true: the beliefs and principles people are taught, which can be true or false. The word can also mean the act of teaching.
To want something very strongly. It becomes sinful when you long for something that belongs to someone else or that you should not have.
