A legion was a big group of Roman soldiers, about 6,000 men. In the Bible it also means a very large number, like a huge crowd or army.
A persecutor is someone who treats another person badly and unfairly again and again, often because of what that person believes.
A Gileadite was a descendant of Gilead. These people were a family group within the tribe of Manasseh, and the word names a person connected to that family.
An Ishmaelite is someone from the family of Ishmael, who lived after him. In Genesis, the traders who bought Joseph from his brothers are called Ishmaelites, and they are also called Midianites.
To step in and plead for someone else, or to act between people to help settle a problem between them.
Bel was the main god of the Babylonians. His name is the Babylonian form of Baal and means "lord."

Condemnation is the act of declaring someone guilty and sentencing them to punishment. It can also mean the punishment-bound position of someone who has been judged guilty, or strong blame for something wrong.
Confessing means openly admitting that something is wrong or true. In these verses, people are owning up to their sins, and Daniel also admits the sins of his whole people, Israel.
Gnashing is grinding or striking the teeth together. People do it when they feel great pain, sadness, or anger.
The place of the dead, the unseen world where all who die go. It is the Greek word for the Hebrew Sheol, and some verses use it for a very low state.
The edge or border of a piece of clothing, often folded over and sewn so the cloth will not come apart.
To hem in means to surround something and shut it in so it cannot get out or get away.
The Messiah is God's promised King, chosen to save His people. The word means "anointed one," and in Greek it is "Christ."
Stubble is the short stumps of grain plants like wheat or barley that stay in the ground after the stalks have been cut down.
People who break a law or disobey a command. A transgressor is someone who does not follow a rule he knows he should keep, so he is a sinner.
Something kept in the high priest's breastpiece, whose name means "Lights." Through it, God let His will be known at certain times, though no one is sure what it was.
Reproof is blame or criticism for a fault, like a scolding that tells someone they did wrong. It can also mean the sharp words of censure or rebuke given to a person.
A spiritist is a person who claims to deal with spirits. The Bible warns God's people not to go to spiritists for help or answers.
To desecrate something is to take away its sacred purpose or treat it as holy no longer. It means using it in a way that is unworthy, the opposite of setting it apart as sacred.
Someone who stands against Christ or tries to take His place. John uses it for false teachers who deny that Jesus Christ came as a real human being.
A charioteer is a person who drives a chariot. In the Bible, charioteers drove the war chariots used in battle.
A strong fenced pen where sheep are gathered and kept safe. It is a place where sheep are collected or shut in, so they are protected.
A doorkeeper is a person who guards the entrance to a house or building and watches who goes in. In the Bible, doorkeepers served at God's house, and some watched the door of a home.
A person from the tribe of Ephraim, one of the tribes of Israel. Ephraimites are also sometimes called Ephrathites.
In one place, the phrase "leaders of the Ephraimites" refers to the leaders of Israel's northern kingdom.
A pagan is someone who worships false gods or idols instead of the one true God. The word can also describe things connected with that kind of worship, like pagan priests.
A pagan is also a person outside God's people, someone who is not a believer. The word can be used in a broad way for those who do not follow God.
In Amos, "pagan" describes land that is unclean, meaning it is not set apart for God.
A race of tall, fierce giants who lived around Hebron in southern Canaan. They terrified the Israelite spies, and Joshua drove most of them out.
The people who lived in Babylon and the land around it, also called Chaldeans. Some of them were moved by the Assyrians to live in the cities of Samaria.
Royal guards who served King David. They carried out death sentences and also carried messages, and some think they were hired foreign soldiers, maybe Philistines.
Time that goes on without end. It can mean time with no beginning and no end, like God's life, or time that starts and then goes on forever into the future.
A goddess is a female god.
A shout that first meant "Save us now!" and became a joyful cry of praise to God, used by the crowds as they welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem.
A lawyer was a person trained in the laws, whose work was to speak for others in court cases and to advise them about their legal rights.
Having leprosy, a skin disease. In the Bible, the Hebrew word was used for several kinds of skin disease, and the skin could look covered with white scales.
Mandrakes are a low plant from the potato family, with purple flowers and sweet-smelling yellow or orange fruit. Its Hebrew name means "love-plants."
The headquarters of a Roman governor, where he lived and worked. It could be a palace or other grand building, and Roman soldiers stayed there too.
Restitution is the act of making a wrong right. You give back what you took from someone, or pay for the loss or damage you caused.
Restitution can also mean the payment or thing itself that is given back to make up for what was lost, harmed, or taken.
In a right and fair way. It is often used for judging people, as in deciding things justly and treating everyone equally.
In a right and just way. To walk righteously means to live your life in a morally right way, doing what is just and fair.
A person who scatters seed so that plants will grow.
Vindication is defending something and showing it to be right or just, when it has been doubted or blamed. It can also mean proving or standing up for a person's right, claim, or cause.
Vindication is proof that someone or something is just and right. When God brings or proclaims it, He declares a cause or action to be just and sets right a wrong.
Something pretty worn or added to make a person or thing look more beautiful, like jewelry. In the Bible, ornaments include bracelets, necklaces, and earrings.
To whip someone hard with a lash as a punishment, or the whip itself. Scourges were often made of leather cords, and some had sharp bits of metal to make the pain worse.
A punishment or terrible trouble that causes great suffering. It can be something sent to correct people, or a disaster that sweeps through and harms them.
A tassel is a hanging decoration made of loose threads or cords tied together at one end. It often hangs from the corners of things like cushions and curtains.
To transgress is to go past a limit by breaking a law or rule that was given. In the Bible it means disobeying God's commands or His covenant, which is sin.
To promise to marry someone, or to be engaged. From the time of the promise, the woman was already treated as the man's lawful wife, even before the wedding.
Used as a picture of the close, spiritual bond between God and His people, as if He were promising to join them to Himself like an engaged couple.
As a word for the person you are engaged to, the one promised to you as a future husband or wife.
An enchanter is a sorcerer or magician, someone who claims to do amazing things by using spirits or demons. The word can also mean someone who charms or delights people.
The Persians were the people who lived in Persia. A Persian is a person from Persia, or something that belongs to that land or its language.
A precious, very valuable blue stone, probably lapis lazuli in Bible times. It was set in the high priest's breastplate, and the word can also mean its deep blue color.
To sift is to pass something through a sieve, a tool with tiny holes, so the fine bits fall through and the coarse bits stay. It can also mean to examine closely.
To beat grain to get the seeds out of the stalks. People did this with oxen's feet or a heavy frame with rollers.
In the Bible, threshing is also a picture of violence and destruction, like crushing enemies or nations with great force.
Guilty of adultery, which means being unfaithful to a husband or wife. In the Bible, it can also describe people who are unfaithful to God, or who are idolatrous or very wicked.

Balm is a sweet-smelling, sticky gum that oozes from certain trees or shrubs. People in Bible lands prized it as medicine for healing, and merchants traded it, like the caravan going from Gilead to Egypt.
Balsam is a thick, sweet-smelling, sticky substance that comes from certain plants. The word is also used as a name for some kinds of plants and trees.
Behemoth is a huge, powerful animal that God made. It is most likely the hippopotamus, a giant river animal that lives in the water and eats plants on land.
A blasphemer is a person who speaks about God in a disrespectful, wicked way. In Leviticus, the word is linked to a man who cursed.
Curds are the thick, lumpy part of milk that separates from the watery part. People ate them as food, and they could also be made into cheese.
Dross is the worthless scum that rises off metal when it is melted, and it is thrown away. The Bible also uses it for cheap, impure metal and for worthless things.
A plant with thin stalks and blue flowers. Its fibers were made into thread and linen cloth, and it was grown in Egypt and Palestine.
A precious gemstone that comes in different colors. It was one of twelve stones on the high priest's breastpiece, and the Bible also describes it as shining and clear like crystal.
A lamentation is any way of showing deep sorrow, such as crying out in grief or wailing. It can be spoken, sung, or written, and it often goes along with mourning.
Papyrus is a tall, reedlike plant with a thick, three-sided stem. It grew in Egypt, and long ago people pressed its stems into a material to write on.
A hard, flat floor or surface made of stones or bricks, laid down so people can walk on it easily. In John, it is a place in Pilate's court paved with colored stones.
Pentecost was a Jewish harvest festival, also called the Feast of Weeks, held on the fiftieth day after Passover. People thanked God and brought Him the first of their grain.
Treating people cruelly and trying to hurt them over and over, especially because of what they believe or how they worship. It can even mean punishing them or putting them to death.
To decide something ahead of time. When the Bible says God predestined people, it means He planned and decided beforehand what would happen for them.
Seraphim are heavenly beings, a kind of angel, that Isaiah saw in a vision standing above God's throne. The name means "burning ones," and they have wings and seemed to look somewhat like people.
Showbread was special bread the priests set out before the Lord in His holy place. There were twelve loaves for the twelve tribes of Israel, replaced every Sabbath.
Shuhite is a name for Bildad, one of Job's friends. It probably shows he came from the family of Shuah, a family line or people group.
A span is a short length of measure. It is the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger when the hand is stretched wide, about nine inches.
A span can also mean a length of time, from beginning to end. It can be a short stretch of time, such as the span of a life.
To span is to stretch across a space or a stretch of time, reaching from one end to the other. It can also mean to measure something with the hand stretched wide.
Stoning was a form of punishment where people threw stones at someone. The Bible says it was ordered for certain offences, and it is also how Stephen and others were harmed.
A taskmaster is a boss who gives people their work and makes them do it, watching over them as an overseer. In Exodus, the Egyptians used taskmasters to burden the Israelites with hard labor.
A tetrarch was a ruler under the Romans. The word first meant the ruler of a fourth part of a region, but it came to mean any ruler of a region.
Thummim is a Hebrew word meaning "perfections." It went with the Urim in the high priest's breastpiece, and God used them to guide Israel, but no one knows exactly what they were.
A name for Elijah the prophet. It probably shows that he came from a place called Tishbi, though sources are not sure where it was, perhaps in Gilead or in Upper Galilee.
A person who studies and thinks deeply about nature, right and wrong, and how to live wisely. A philosopher is someone devoted to learning and wisdom.
To make up for a wrong, sin, or crime by paying for it or making amends. The word also carries the idea of reconciling, or bringing together those who were set apart by the offense.
A piece of armor that covered and protected a soldier's chest. The Bible also uses it as a picture of things like righteousness, faith and love that guard a person.
To pervert something is to twist it away from what is true or right, so it is used the wrong way. It can also mean to lead someone astray.
To point out that someone is wrong, often to help him change. It can be done calmly, and it means showing him his fault.
To grind or strike the teeth together. People did this when they were very angry, or when they were in great pain or sorrow.
A small plant with seeds like tiny flat beans, grown in pods. The seeds were used for food, such as stew or bread, and people still enjoy them in many places.
A perfumer is a person whose job is to make or sell perfumes, which are sweet-smelling things.
A sweet-smelling and costly wood, or the perfume made from it, probably brought from India. It was used as perfume and also to prepare the bodies of the dead for burial.
An archangel is a chief angel, a leader among the angels. The Bible uses this word only twice, and many people believe it means a created being, though a very highly honored one.
Ashtoreths are statues or forms of Ashtoreth, the main female goddess of the Phoenicians. She was often worshiped with the male god Baal, and Israel sinned by worshiping her.
Bondage is slavery, when people are forced to serve others and are not free. The Bible uses it for Israel's hard slavery in Egypt, and for later times of captivity and rule by foreign kings.
"Christs" means more than one person claiming to be the Christ, the Anointed One, God's chosen Savior. "False Christs" are people who pretend to be Him but are not.
A small plant grown for its seeds, which taste warm and a little bitter and smell spicy. The seeds are used to flavor food, much like anise and caraway.
A small clay pot filled with things that burn easily, so it holds fire and gives off smoke and flames.
Graven means carved. A graven image is an idol, an object people worshiped that was carved from wood, stone, or similar material.
Judaism is the religion of the Jewish people, with the beliefs and practices given in the laws of Moses. A convert to Judaism is someone who joined this religion.
Kneading is working and pressing dough with the hands until it becomes a well-mixed mass, getting it ready for baking bread. A kneading bowl is the bowl or trough where this is done.
Someone from a place called Naamah. This is the name used for Zophar, one of Job's three friends, and the place was probably in Arabia.
Treating people in a cruel and unfair way, or loading them down with burdens that are too heavy for them to bear.
Purim is a Jewish festival that remembers how the Jews were saved from Haman's plan to destroy them. Its name means "lots," because Haman cast lots to choose the day.
A reaper is a person who cuts grain when it is ripe, using a sickle, which is a curved tool for cutting grain. Reapers do the work of bringing in the harvest.
Recompense is something given back for what a person has done or suffered. It can be a reward for good or a punishment for wrong, and from God it is what He gives in return.
Sovereign means having the highest power and authority, with no one above or over you. When it describes God, it means He is the supreme ruler, in charge of everything.
Sovereignty is the right and power to rule with the highest authority, like a king. When it is about God, it means He has the right to do everything as He pleases.
A zealot is someone who cares very strongly about something and works hard for it. Simon, one of Jesus' twelve followers, is called the Zealot.
A dignitary is a person who has an important rank or a position of honor. The word can also mean a church leader with a higher rank than an ordinary priest.
An exhortation is words meant to encourage and urge people to do what is good. It can be advice or a warning that pushes someone toward right living.
An idolater is someone who worships idols, which are images or statues made by human hands, or who worships anything as a god that is not the true God.
An omer is a dry measure, used in Exodus to measure manna. It equals about 2 dry quarts (2.2 liters) and is one-tenth of an ephah.
A patriarch is the father and head of a family or tribe who ruled it with a father's authority. The word is used especially for Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Jacob's twelve sons.
A very high part of the temple in Jerusalem where the devil set Jesus. It was probably a wing-shaped part above the roof, high over the valley below.
A tall, pointed part of a building that rises up higher than the rest, like a turret or the top of a tower.
The sharp metal blade of a plow. It cuts into the earth and lifts the soil so the farmer can turn it over before planting.
A rampart is a strong wall or high bank of earth built around a city or fort to protect it from attackers. It can also mean anything that keeps people safe.
A large shade tree related to the fig, with leaves like a mulberry's. Its sweet fruit grows right on the trunk and branches, and its wide branches are easy to climb.
To fathom something is to understand it fully, getting to the bottom of it, like measuring how deep water is. People use it for things too deep or big to grasp.
A fathom is a length of six feet, about how far a man can stretch out his arms. Sailors used it to measure how deep the water was.
Someone from Nazareth, the town where Jesus lived. It was used for Jesus, sometimes as an insulting name, and enemies also used it for His followers.
A pitcher is a container for holding liquids like water or wine. In Bible lands, people often carried pitchers on the head or shoulder, and some were made of clay with handles.
Atoning means making things right after a wrong has been done, by paying for it or making up for it. It brings people back into friendship, or agreement, with those they have wronged.
The Babylonian name King Nebuchadnezzar gave to the prophet Daniel. It is thought to mean something like "Bel protect his life," naming a Babylonian god.
Beryl is a hard, beautiful gemstone, often green or bluish-green. A beryl was set in the high priest's breastplate, and the Bible uses its gleam to describe shining things in visions.
Caraway is a plant in the parsley family. Its seeds have a strong, pleasant smell and a warm, sharp taste, and people used them in cooking and in medicine.
A diadem is a special band or crown worn on the head as a sign of royalty. It was a mark of kings, and it could also be a beautiful ornament.
The holy diadem was a gold plate that Moses fastened to the front of Aaron's turban. It was a special part of the priest's clothing, not a royal crown.
A gift or payment of money that a man gave to the father of the woman he wanted to marry, before she could become his wife.
Money, goods, or property given along with a bride when she married. Here a father gives it to his daughter as her wedding gift.
Gall is something very bitter, like the bitter fluid called bile from the liver or a bitter, poisonous plant. In the Bible it often stands for bitterness and suffering.
A broad, shallow pan, often made of iron, used for baking or frying cakes. In these verses, grain offerings of flour and oil were cooked on it.
The part of a ruler's house where the women lived, kept apart from other people. It can also mean the women of one man's household.
A headband is a band worn around the head. It is also called a fillet.
Hypocrisy is pretending to be good or religious when you really are not, hiding what you are truly like inside. It is a false show of goodness.
Not clean under the religious law of Moses. The BSB footnote says the Greek word literally means "common," and God tells Peter not to call impure what He has made clean.
Made dirty by sin or guilt, especially by wrong and shameful actions or words. Such a person is not holy.
A Moabitess is a woman from the people of Moab, or a woman who is a Moabite. Ruth is called this because she came from the land of Moab.
An outcast is someone who has been forced out of their home, country, or group and is treated as rejected or unwanted.
A group of soldiers who served as King David's bodyguards and are always named with the Cherethites. The name probably means "runners" or "couriers," so they may also have carried messages.
A long journey, especially one made to a holy place to worship. In the Bible, it can also mean the journey of a person's whole life.
A Roman ruler sent to govern a region far from Rome. He was picked from Rome's top group of leaders and served for one year, handling everyday matters like laws and order.
Reptiles are animals that crawl on their bellies, like snakes, or move on very short legs, like lizards.
A tribe descended from Seba, known as tall "men of stature" who traded goods. Another group in Job 1:15 seems to have been raiders, and Joel 3:8 means people from Sheba.
A person who lived in Shiloh. In the Bible, this name is used for the prophet Ahijah, whose home was Shiloh.
A Shunammite is a person from Shunem. In the Bible, Abishag and another woman in the cards are both called Shunammites because that was where they were from.
Syrophoenician may mean someone with one Phoenician parent and one Syrian parent. Or it may mean a Phoenician from the Roman province of Syria, not from Africa.
A graceful tree or shrub with long, feathery branches and very tiny leaves. In spring it has spikes of small pink flowers that can cover the whole tree.
Someone who tries to pull people into doing wrong. In the Bible, the Tempter is the Devil, the great enemy who tries to lead people into evil.
Uncircumcision is the state of not being circumcised, which is the opposite of circumcision. The word can also mean people who are not circumcised, meaning the Gentiles.
Unrighteous describes someone who is not righteous. This kind of person does what is evil, wicked, or sinful, and does not live by God's law.
Unrighteousness is wrongdoing or injustice, breaking God's law and the basic rules of fairness. It can be one wrong act, but often it means a habit of wickedness.
Winnowing is separating grain from its light outer covering, called chaff. Farmers threw the grain up into the evening wind, and the wind blew the chaff away.
A fowler is a hunter who catches or kills wild birds for food. Fowlers set traps and snares to catch them.
The outer edge or border of something. In this verse, the fringes of God's ways are just the outer edge, a small part of all He does.
A decorated edge on a piece of clothing, made of loose threads or cords. God told Israel to wear them on their cloaks to remind them of His commands.
A Korahite is a descendant of Korah, from the Kohathite family of Levites. Korahites worked as singers and doorkeepers at the temple, and one was in charge of baking for the offerings.
A small copper or bronze coin used in Bible times. It was worth very little, only a tiny part of a denarius, which was about a day's pay.
A cor was a large measuring container, round in shape, used for both dry things like flour and wheat and for liquids. Early writers guessed it held about 45 to 87 gallons.
An evangelist is a traveling preacher who shares the good news about Jesus, especially in places that have not heard it. An evangelist is much like a missionary.
A firebrand is a piece of wood that is burning, like a torch or a stick with a glowing end. In the Bible it can also mean a burning arrow or dart.
Under a curse, and so doomed to suffering or destruction. It can also mean so wicked or hateful that a person or thing deserves to be cursed.
A soft, white stone that looks like marble and is easy to carve. It was made into jars for keeping perfume and ointment, so an alabaster jar was a container for perfume.
Apostleship is the job and honor of being an apostle. It is a special position given to a person to serve in that role.
Archite is the name always given to Hushai, David's faithful friend. It may show where Hushai came from, but no one is sure exactly what it means.
Punishing someone who has done wrong, to make things right for an injury. When God does it, He is standing up for what is right and punishing those who do wrong.
The intestines, or guts, inside the body of a person or animal. This is the body part meant in these verses.
A person or group that others talk about and make fun of. It can also mean a common saying, and the word is used for someone people speak of with contempt.
People who have turned from one religion to another. In these verses, converts are people who changed their beliefs, and the card for Acts shows they turned to Judaism.
People whose hearts were changed so they stopped following sin and began to love God and live for Him.
A strong pot used to melt metals such as silver, or ores, in very hot fire. The word can also mean a hard test or trial that shows what something is really like.
Debauchery is living with no self-control and giving in too much to what the body wants. It especially means going too far in lustful, sexual behavior.
A dirge is a sad song or tune that shows grief and sorrow, especially one sung at a funeral.
A dynasty is a line of kings from the same family, one ruler after another. It can also mean the rule of that royal family over a country.
Filigree is decorative work made from fine wire, usually attached to gold or silver. The wire is shaped into delicate, detailed designs.
The Gerasenes were the people who lived in a region on the far side of the lake from Galilee. Some old Bible copies call them Gadarenes or Gergesenes instead.
A Grecian Jew was a Jewish person who spoke Greek. Many came from other lands, and they are set apart from the Hebrew-speaking Jews.
Hardening is the act of making something hard or harder. Here it means becoming unfeeling, like a heart that has grown stubborn and will not give in.
In the Bible, a hearth was a place for a fire or for heating things. It was not like a modern fireplace but could be hot ashes, a pan of coals, or burning fuel.
A hin was a Hebrew measure for liquids like oil, wine, and water. It held a little less than one gallon, or about 3.7 liters.
Having to do with idolatry, which is worshiping idols or false gods instead of the true God. An idolatrous person, place, or thing is tied up with that false worship.
Jashar is part of the name of a book mentioned in the Bible, the Book of Jashar. The footnote says the name can also mean the Book of the Upright One.
A special, loving name for the people of Israel. It means "the upright one," which is someone who does what is right, and it shows how dearly loved Israel was.
Malchishua was one of King Saul's sons, and his name means "king of help." He died with his father in the battle at Gilboa.
The regular time when a woman's body passes out blood and fluid, called the menses. The word can mean the flow itself or the days it lasts.
Nard is a sweet-smelling plant from the East that people long ago prized. A costly perfume or ointment was also made from it, and the Bible uses both senses.
A name given to Shemaiah, a false prophet who went with the captives to Babylon. No one knows where the name came from, but a side note translates it "dreamer."
A group in the early church whose evil deeds were strongly condemned. They likely ate food offered to idols and took part in sexual sin, while still claiming to follow Christ.
The Ninevites were the people who lived in Nineveh.
Orion is a bright group of about eighty stars in the sky, called a constellation. Some old traditions pictured it as a giant, and the Arabs linked that giant to Nimrod.
Paradise is a word that first meant a beautiful garden or park. In the Bible it names the happy place of rest and joy where God's people are with Him after death.
A group of stars close together in the sky, found near the shoulder of the constellation Taurus. The Bible points to them as something God made.
Reconciliation is becoming friends again after people have been apart or against each other. In the Bible, it is how sinners are brought back into friendship and favor with God.
Reigning means ruling as a king, with the highest power over a land and its people. A reigning ruler holds that power at the time being talked about.
Remembrance is keeping something in mind, or bringing it back to mind. It can also be something that helps people remember, like a note, a memorial, or a record.
The scapegoat was a goat chosen on the Day of Atonement. The priest laid the people's sins on it, and it was sent away alive into the wilderness, carrying their guilt with it.
A group of people who follow the same beliefs or way of life and stand apart from others. In the Bible it often means a religious party, like the Pharisees or the followers of Jesus.
Stewardship is the office of a steward, which means the position or job a steward holds. In these verses, it is a job connected to God's grace, a mystery, and His work.
A stylus is a tool for writing. It is shaped like a pen or a needle, and it can be used to make marks or cut lines.
A valuable gemstone, yellowish or greenish in color. It was one of the stones in the high priest's breastplate, and Job says it came from Cush.
To be transfigured is to have your outward look changed into something glorious. Jesus was transfigured when His face shone like the sun and His clothes turned bright white.
Undefiled means not made dirty or spoiled. It describes something that is still clean and pure.
Extra payment, like interest, that a lender asks for on top of a loan of money or food. God's law told the Jews not to charge it to each other.
A Hebrew measure for large amounts of things, such as grain, seed, or even quail. It was the largest measure of its kind, about 220 liters.
The Horites were the early people of Mount Seir in Edom, and their name probably means "cave" because they likely lived in caves. Esau's descendants later drove them out.
Judean means from or having to do with Judea. As a noun, a Judean is a person who comes from Judea, a Jew.
Perversity is being perverse: a stubborn, cranky, contrary way of acting or speaking that likes to thwart and cross others instead of going along.
A seah was a Jewish way to measure dry things like flour or grain. It held a little over one peck, which is about as much as a small bucket of apples.
A comforter is someone who brings comfort and support to a person who is sad, hurting, or in trouble, helping them feel stronger.
Intercession is praying or pleading for other people, asking God to meet their needs. Jesus and the Holy Spirit do this for believers, and believers can do it for each other.
Algum is a kind of wood from a tree, probably another spelling of almug. No one is sure which tree it was, but it may have been a gummy wood.
Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet. When God calls Himself the Alpha and the Omega, the last letter, it shows He is eternal, covering the beginning and the end.
The Athenians were the people who were born in or lived in Athens, an important city in Greece.
A backslider is someone who falls away from his faith and the practice of religion. It can also mean a person who neglects his promises to obey God and falls into sin.
Blaspheming means speaking about God or holy things with disrespect, or saying insulting, hateful words against Him.
Showing great disrespect toward God, or speaking about Him in a way that is rude and insulting. Blasphemous words or names show a lack of respect for God.
The Carites were a group of men named with the commanders and guards. A Bible note says the word may mean mercenaries, who are paid soldiers, or executioners.
Constellations are groups of stars that look close together in the sky. People gave them shapes, like a bear or a bull, to help sort and remember them.
Contrite means feeling deep sorrow for doing wrong, because it displeases God. A contrite person is humble and truly sorry, like a heart that has been broken.
A debtor is a person who owes something to someone else, usually money. The one who is owed is called the creditor.
A debtor can also be a person who is under an obligation to do something. In the Lord's Prayer, debtors are people who owe us because they have wronged us.
The Dispersion means God's people who were scattered to many lands outside Israel. In James, it points to Jewish believers living far from their homeland.
God's choice of certain people to be the objects of His mercy and grace. It is His own choosing, not something earned, and it can be about individuals or a group like Israel.
A title given to two men in the Bible, Ethan and Heman. Both were sons of Zerah.
A goad is a long rod with a sharp point that farmers used to poke oxen and make them move. "Kicking against the goad" meant fighting a stronger power, which never works.
To heave something is to lift it up or raise it with a big effort, especially when it is heavy and hard to move. It can also mean to throw something.
A good, fair reason that shows an action was right or allowed. In this verse, the city has no good reason to explain the crowd's uproar.
God's act of forgiving the sins of people who trust in Jesus and treating them as right with Him. It is the opposite of condemnation.
Kindred can also mean a whole clan or people who share the same ancestors, a bigger group than just your close family.
A name meaning "bitter," or sad. Naomi chose it for herself in Ruth 1:20 because of the hard and painful things that had happened to her.
Nacon is a name connected with a threshing floor. The footnote says it is a variant of Chidon, the name used in 1 Chronicles 13:9.
Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet. In the phrase "the Alpha and the Omega," it means the last and the end, so God is the beginning and the ending of all things.
A wild bird of the rocky hills that calls loudly in the morning. It runs instead of flying, so hunters could tire it out and knock it down.
Pastors are leaders who care for a church and its people, like shepherds caring for a flock. They watch over the people and teach them about the Christian faith.
Profaning something holy means treating it with disrespect, as if it were ordinary, or making it unclean. In these verses, people profane the Sabbath by not honoring it as the sacred day it is.
A refiner is a worker who melts metal like silver or gold in a hot furnace to separate the pure metal from the waste. In the Bible, this picture shows God making His people pure.
Having to do with sacrifice, which is an offering given in worship. Something sacrificial is used in making a sacrifice or is part of one.
Spelt is a kind of grain in the wheat family, also called German wheat. It was grown as a food crop.
Swaddling cloths are bands or cloths wrapped around a baby, especially a newborn. The baby is bound up snugly in them.
Swine are pigs or hogs. The Law of Moses called them unclean and forbade eating them, and in Matthew 7:6 they stand for people who treat holy and wise things with disrespect.
A tree also called the turpentine tree. It grows in great numbers in the south and east of Palestine.
Tongs are a metal tool with two long arms joined at one end. People use them to pick up things that are too hot to touch, like burning coals.
Ungodliness is living as if God does not matter. It means ignoring Him and His commands, not honoring Him, and doing wrong or disrespectful things against Him.
Having harm or trouble come upon a person. Here, the one who fears the LORD rests content and is not visited by harm.
A time when God comes to judge people and punish them for their sins. It is also called a day of punishment.
A yokefellow is a close partner or companion who shares in the work. In Philippians 4:3, Paul calls someone his true yokefellow, and a footnote says this may be a man named Syzygus.
An Abiezrite was a person from the family that came from a man named Abiezer. The name is said to mean "father of help."
A buckler is a shield that a soldier carried on his arm to protect his body in battle. Old ones were made of wood or leather, and some had metal plates added for strength.
A follower of Jesus Christ. The name was first used at Antioch, probably by outsiders who looked down on the disciples, who called themselves brothers, disciples, and saints.
To dispossess someone is to take away what they have, such as land or a crown, so they no longer hold it. The dispossessed are people this has happened to.
An Elamite was a person from Elam, an ancient kingdom in southwestern Asia that later became part of Persia. Elamites were descendants of Shem, and the name may come from a man named Elam.
A partaker is someone who shares in something together with others, taking a part of it, like a gift, a promise, or a blessing.
A terrible disease that spreads among many people and harms or kills a great number of them. It is also called a plague.
Someone or something that is harmful and spreads bad effects to many people. Here it is a word of insult for a person accused of causing trouble.
A hollow place in the body or in an object that holds something else. Examples are the hollow where an eyeball sits or where a tooth fits.
A vat is a large tub or tank for holding liquids, like wine, while they are still being made.
To winnow is to separate grain from its light outer bits, called chaff. People tossed the grain into the wind with a shovel, sometimes using a fan too, and the wind blew the chaff away.
To winnow can also mean to sift out and separate the bad from the good, or to scatter. In Jeremiah 51:2, enemies winnow Babylon and empty her land.
Abstinence means choosing on purpose to hold back from something, like certain foods or drinks, instead of enjoying it. It is a kind of self-denial.
A name given to Haman and also to his father. It may mean Haman belonged to a group of people called the Amalekites, or it may point to his family background.
Someone from the family line of Ahoah. The name was used for some of David's warriors, like Eleazar, because they were descendants of Ahoah.
Alms are gifts of money, food, or clothing given freely to help poor people. Giving alms is an act of kindness and charity toward those in need.
Almug is a kind of wood that ships brought from a land called Ophir. It was used to build parts of the temple and for other things, and some think it was sandalwood.
Apostasies are times when people give up the faith or beliefs they once openly claimed as their own. They completely turn away from what they had professed.
The Ashdodites were the people who lived in Ashdod.
A family or group of people whose name may mean "people of the wells." They followed Sheba, but no one knows for sure who they were.
A bier is a frame or stand used to carry a dead body to the grave. Its shape and decoration could be plainer or fancier depending on who the person was.
A nickname Jesus gave to James and John. It means "Sons of Thunder," probably because they were so fiery, eager, and quick to act.
A name given to Elihu in the book of Job. He was probably called this because he was a descendant of Buz, though the source says this is only likely.
Cassia is a sweet-smelling spice made from the inner bark of a tree like the cinnamon tree. It was brought from India and was one of the spices in God's holy anointing oil.
Cassia here is a sweet-smelling spice used to perfume clothes. It was probably made from the peeled bark of a tree like the cinnamon tree.
To chastise is to punish someone, often with pain, so they will stop doing wrong and return to doing right. In these verses, God says He will do this.
Chislev was a month in the Hebrew year, which is based on the moon's cycles. It was the ninth month and came around late autumn, in November and December.
A plant grown for its small, round seeds, which are about the size of a peppercorn. The seeds smell strong and are used to add flavor, and manna looked like them.
Coveting is wanting something so strongly that you long for what you should not have, like something that belongs to someone else. It puts your heart on things instead of on God.
Covetous means wanting something too much, being overly eager to get and keep things, especially money or goods. It is a wrong kind of wanting.
Defilement is being made dirty or unclean, either in body or in heart. It can also mean being spoiled by sin, so that something is no longer pure.
Demonic means having to do with a demon or with demons.
A deputy is someone chosen to act in place of another person, using that person's power. In the Bible, one deputy ruled Edom in place of a king.
Dill is a plant whose seeds are warming, sharp-tasting, and sweet-smelling. In the past, people used the seeds as a soothing medicine for children.
A stick that holds a bunch of soft plant or animal fibers, like wool. Thread is pulled from it by hand while a spindle twists the fibers into thread.
A drachma was a silver coin used by the ancient Greeks. It was worth about one day's wages for a worker.
A sickness where extra water builds up in the body and makes part of it swell. In Luke 14, Jesus healed a man who had it on the Sabbath.
A word Jesus cried out on the cross, which the verse says means "My God." The dictionary says it is a Syro-Chaldaic form of "Eli," another way of saying the same words.
To treat a dead body with spices, oils, and other special substances so it will not rot. The Egyptians did this, and Joseph's servants did it for his father Israel.
An Aramaic word that means "Be opened." Jesus spoke it when He healed a man who could not hear or speak well.
Exaltation is being lifted up to a high place, such as a position of power, honor, or greatness. It is also the act of raising someone up like this.
Exorcists were people who tried to force evil spirits out of others by using God's name, special words, and ceremonies. Many were Jews, but they were pretenders who did not truly have power.
Fallow land is a field that is not planted for a season or more. Farmers plow it but sow no seed, which helps kill weeds and soften the soil.
A firepan was a shallow metal dish used in worship. It likely held burning coals for incense, which gives off sweet-smelling smoke, or caught the burned ends of wicks cut off the lamps.
Foreknowledge is knowing something before it happens. It is a special part of who God is: He knows the future and what will happen in it.
The people who lived in the region around Gadara, a city southeast of the Sea of Galilee. Some Bible copies call them Gergesenes or Gerasenes, and the area had many tomb caves.
The people of Geshur, who lived east of the Jordan River. They stayed on friendly terms with the Israelites.
A tribe who lived in the south-west of the land, near its border. They were one of the early peoples already living there.
One of the tribes living in the land of Canaan before the Israelites came. They were descendants of Canaan's fifth son, and were part of the larger Hivite family.
Godlessness is being impious or irreligious. It describes a person who lacks reverence for God and does not follow religion.
A handbreadth is a short measure about as wide as four fingers, roughly four inches. In this verse, days that are handbreadths means life is very short.
Hebraic means having to do with the Hebrews or with the language of the Hebrews. In this verse, the Hebraic Jews are the Jews linked to the Hebrews.
The Hebronites were a family group of Levites from the Kohath branch. They were descendants of a man named Hebron.
Henna is a thorny shrub with sweet-smelling white flowers. Its leaves can be ground into a powder that makes a red dye, used in the East to color nails and fingers.
Heresies are teachings people choose for themselves that are not from God. They turn away from the basic truth of the gospel, and the Bible says they lead to destruction.

Ingathering means gathering in the crops from the fields at harvest time. The Feast of Ingathering was a yearly celebration, also called Sukkot or the Feast of Tabernacles, when the people went to Jerusalem.
Kenizzite was the name of a tribe mentioned in God's promise to Abraham. Caleb is called a Kenizzite, which seems to show he was linked to this tribe.
The Libyans were people from Libya, an old name for the land in northern Africa west of Egypt. In the Bible, they appear as soldiers and as a people.
Menstrual describes something that has to do with the monthly bleeding a woman's body goes through. It comes from a word meaning "month," because it happens about once a month.
Nehushtan is the name for the bronze snake Moses made in the wilderness, meaning "a bronze thing." The people began to treat it like an idol and burned incense to it.
The Nephilim were giants. The word is a Hebrew name left untranslated in the Bible, and it is used for these giant people in Genesis and again in Numbers.
Nisan was the first month of the Hebrew calendar, which follows the moon. It fell in March and April, and the name may come from a word meaning "beginning."
Nisroch was a false god of Assyria. King Sennacherib was worshiping in this god's temple when his sons killed him, and some think the god was shown with an eagle's head.
Pasturing means taking animals out to eat the grass that grows on the ground. It also means giving them grass land to feed on.
A pavilion is a large tent that can be moved, often used by a king or general. The Bible pictures God's pavilion as the dark clouds and waters of the sky around Him.
People who help those who are fighting or disagreeing make peace with each other.
Large, beautiful birds with very long, colorful tail feathers. They come from India, and Solomon's ships brought them home from far away along with gold, silver and ivory.
Perjurers are people who willfully tell a lie after taking a lawful oath. Someone who breaks an oath in any way can also be called a perjurer.
Perpetual means never stopping and lasting forever. Something perpetual has no end and will not go away.
A pestle is a tool for pounding and breaking things in a mortar. In this verse, it is used to picture grinding grain.
A potsherd is a broken piece of a clay pot. It is a fragment of earthenware, left over when a pot is smashed.
A prefect was a high official who governed or was in charge of a city, province, or department. In Daniel, they are among the leaders King Nebuchadnezzar gathers together.
A very respectful title that people used when speaking to a teacher. It was thought to be the most honorable title of all, and John 20:16 says it means "Teacher."
Redeeming means buying something back or rescuing it by paying a price. It can also mean making good on something by doing it fully, or making up for a loss.
To rend is to tear or split something apart with force. In Isaiah 64:1, the people ask God to tear open the heavens and come down in power and greatness.
To rend is to tear something apart, and people tore their clothes to show deep sadness or sorrow for sin. To rend the heart means to feel bitter sorrow inside, not just show it outside.
Repentant describes a person who is sorry for the wrong they have done. In this verse, "repentant ones" means people who feel sorrow for their sin.
Reviled means spoken to or about with mean, insulting words that showed disrespect. Those who reviled Zion insulted her.
An Aramaic word that means "You have left Me" or "You have abandoned Me." Jesus spoke it on the cross as part of His loud cry.
This is the way the Ephraimites pronounced the word Shibboleth. It is a different way of saying the same word.
Stadia are a way of measuring distance. The footnote says 1,600 stadia is about 184 miles, or 296 kilometers, and 12,000 stadia is about 1,380 miles, or 2,220 kilometers.
People who make tents for a living. Paul's trade may have been making tent-cloth, and some think he made tents from goatskins.
People who came from Tyre. In this verse, the Tyrians were the people of Tyre who brought cedar logs to David.
Unrepentant describes something that has not been repented of, which means it has not been felt sorry for or turned away from. In the verse, it describes a heart that has not done this.
Usurpers are people who take something, like a throne or power, that does not belong to them. They grab it without any right to have it.
Vermilion is a bright red coloring used for painting. People used it to decorate houses and to paint pictures, such as images on walls.
A musical instrument with many wires stretched across a flat sounding-board. The kind described here is played in Austria and Germany, so the one in Daniel may have looked different.
Someone from Alexandria, a city in Egypt, or something that belongs to that city. In Acts, Alexandrians were Jews from there who had a synagogue, a Jewish place of worship, in Jerusalem.
To chasten is to correct someone by causing them pain or trouble, so that they will change for the better. It is a kind of discipline, like a parent correcting a child.
A fatling is a young animal, like a calf or lamb, that is fed well to make it fat. It was raised to be killed for food or offered as a sacrifice.
The loose fold of skin that covers the tip of the penis.
To pacify is to calm someone who is angry, or to calm the anger or wrath itself, so that it settles down and becomes quiet.
A soothsayer is someone who claims to tell what will happen in the future, but without help from God. Some tried to read the clouds or stars.
A word for "father" that shows warm love and trust. In the New Testament it is used when speaking to God as Father.
To adjure someone is to give them a very serious command or strongly urge them to do something, sometimes calling on them to make a serious promise.
An Adullamite is a person who lives in the city of Adullam. Hirah, the man Judah settled near, came from there.
The parts that were connected to a baby inside its mother. They come out of the mother's body after the baby is born.
An Ammonitess is a woman from the Ammonite people. They were a nation that came from Lot's family line through his son Ben-ammi, and they lived east of the Jordan River.
An Areopagite was a member of the court, or council, called the Areopagus. Dionysius was one of its members.
Ascension means rising or going up. In the Bible it points to Jesus being taken up visibly into heaven, forty days after He rose from the dead.
An awl is a small tool with a sharp point for poking holes. In the Bible, it was used to pierce the ear of a servant who chose to serve his master for life.
A person whose head is bald. In this verse, the boys use it as a rude name to make fun of Elisha.
Begotten means fathered or brought into being. It describes a child who was brought into existence by a parent.
Belial is a word that means "worthless." In this verse it is a name for Satan, who stands for everything evil.
A Bethlehemite is a person who lives in the town of Bethlehem in Judea.
In a way that shows great disrespect toward God. Someone who does something blasphemously speaks or acts as if God does not deserve honor.
Brazen means bold and shameless, with no embarrassment about doing wrong. The old sources say such a person has a face hard like brass.
Bul is the name of a month, the eighth one on the old Hebrew calendar, which fell in the fall around October and November. Its name is linked to the word for rain.
The Caphtorites were a people who came from a place called Caphtor. The Philistines are said to have come from them.
A hard stone that is deep red, flesh-colored, or reddish white. It can be polished until it shines, and it was often used for seals.
Having to do with a special act done in a set way, especially as part of worship. The word is often used for the worship rules of the Jewish religion.
A trusted helper of a king. Blastus held an honored place close to the king and had great influence with him.
A group of people joined together under one government and set of laws. In this verse, it means the nation of Israel as a community that people belonged to.
Conjurers are people who practice magic and pretend to use a secret, mysterious power to do amazing things, like finding stolen goods.
Conjury is the practice of magic, using spells or enchantments. In this verse, God's people are told not to do it.
Consecrating means setting someone or something apart for God's holy use. In this verse, the Levites were making themselves ready and dedicated to serve God.
A coppersmith is a person whose job is to make things out of copper, such as pots and other tools for the home.
Darics were gold coins made by the Persian kings. Each one showed a king holding a bow, and the Jews used them after they returned from Babylon.
Discipleship is being a disciple, which means following someone and learning what he teaches. In this verse, it describes the kind of tongue God gave the speaker.
Dispossessing means taking away something from someone, especially their land or home, so they no longer have it.
A divining rod is a stick, often with forked branches, used by people who pretend to find hidden water or metals underground. In this verse, the people count on such rods to give them answers.
A sickness of the bowels that causes sharp belly pains and waste with blood and mucus in it. When it is severe, it usually comes with a high fever.
Edification is building someone up in their mind and spirit. It means helping a person grow in knowledge, goodness, and faith through teaching.
To edify is to teach and help someone grow stronger in understanding, faith, and goodness. Here, speaking in a tongue helps oneself grow, while prophesying helps the whole church grow.
Edifying means helping someone learn and grow, especially in faith. Something edifying builds up the mind and teaches in a good way.
Elul was a month in the Jewish year, the sixth one when counted from the spring. It came in late summer, around August and September, and lasted twenty-nine days.
To emasculate means to castrate a male, which makes him unable to have children. It can also mean to take away someone's strength or spirit and make him weak.
Embalming was a way of keeping a dead body from rotting by treating it with sweet-smelling spices and oils. The Egyptians did this very carefully, and Jacob's body was treated this way.
Enmity is deep hatred between enemies, the opposite of friendship. It is stronger than just being annoyed, because this hatred lasts a long time.
A follower of the ideas of Epicurus. In this verse, the Epicurean philosophers were people who followed his way of thinking and argued with Paul.
Ethanim was the seventh month of the old Hebrew calendar, around September and October. Its name means "month of gifts," and it began the everyday year.
Festal means having to do with a feast or holiday. It describes something joyful and happy, like a festal sacrifice offered during a celebration.
A tall tree that grew on Lebanon, with wood used for doors, ceilings, floors, and ship decks. No one is sure which tree this was, maybe a cypress or a pine.
Flogging is whipping someone as a punishment. In this verse, it is one of the hard things that some people endured.
Forbearance is patience shown toward people who do wrong, holding back anger or punishment instead of striking right away. Here, God was patient with sins and delayed His punishment.
A freedman is a man who used to be a slave but has been set free.
Galbanum is a sticky gum from a plant, used as one of the spices in the holy incense. It is brownish-yellow and has a strong smell that people today would not find pleasant.
The Gebalites were the people who lived in Gebal, a place also known as the area of Byblos. Their land was part of the territory still left to be taken.
A gerah was a tiny unit of weight and money used by the Israelites. It took twenty gerahs to equal one shekel.
The Gershomites were a family group of Levites, also spelled Gershonites. In this passage they were given thirteen cities from several tribes.
Goatskins are the skins of goats. The word can also mean leather that is made from goat skin.
Gopher is a kind of wood God told Noah to use for building the ark. It is named only once in the Bible, and many people think it was cypress.
To hallow something is to treat it as holy and special. When people pray that God's name be hallowed, they ask that it be honored and respected as holy.
Hamites were people who came from Ham, one of Noah's sons. In this verse, some of them had lived in that land before the others arrived.
Harlotries are the practice of prostitution, which means having sex for pay. The word also means a habit of lewd living.
A hireling is a worker who is hired for a short time and paid wages. In the Law of Moses, his pay was to be given to him by the end of each day.
An insurrectionist is someone who takes part in an insurrection, or who supports one. That means a person who joins others in rising up against those in power.
Interceding means speaking up or pleading for someone else. Here, Jesus is at God's right hand, pleading for us and acting as a go-between for us with God.
The Izharites were a family group of people who came from a man named Izhar. They were his descendants.
A Jewess is a woman who was born a Hebrew, or Jew, from any tribe. Drusilla, the wife of Felix, was one.
An evergreen shrub or low tree that grows in dry places. It has small bluish berries and hard, reddish wood.
Declaring someone to be in the right and free from blame, the opposite of condemning. Here God would show the righteous man was right by rewarding him.
To work and press dough into a well-mixed mass, usually with the hands. People did this to get dough ready for baking bread.
A laurel is an evergreen tree or shrub with sweet-smelling leaves, also called the bay tree. Its leaves and the tree give a fragrant oil.
A libation is a liquid, usually wine, that people poured out on the ground or on a sacrifice to honor a god. The word can also mean the act of pouring it.
A lotus is a kind of water lily. Long ago in Egypt it was pictured on monuments, and in some lands people used it in religious ceremonies.
Maoch was the father of Achish, the king of Gath, where David went for safety with his six hundred men. His name is also spelled Maacah in 1 Kings 2:39.
The Maonites were one of the enemy peoples who oppressed Israel, listed here with other nations God saved His people from. They may be the same people as the Mehunim.
Meholathite describes someone from a place called Mehola. The Bible uses it for Adriel, son of Barzillai, to show where he came from.
A round garden vegetable with a strong taste, grown underground as a bulb and eaten as food. In the wilderness the Israelites missed the onions of Egypt, which were large and mild.
A sweet-smelling ingredient in the holy incense. It was probably made from the hard lid of a shellfish found in the Red Sea, and it gave off a strong smell when burned.
Wild, out-of-control parties with lots of drinking. The word was used for pagan ceremonies honoring false gods, like the Greek and Roman worship of Bacchus, which were full of noisy, reckless fun.
An oxgoad is a long stick with a pointed end, used to drive oxen. Farmers carried it, but in Judges 3:31 Shamgar used one as a weapon against the Philistines.
Parchments were animal skins, such as sheep or goat skins, that were cleaned and prepared so people could write on them. Paul asked Timothy to bring his parchments.
People from Parthia, a strong ancient land in Asia. Parthians were in Jerusalem at Pentecost, and they were known as skilled archers who shot arrows while riding fast.
Petitioning means asking for something in a humble, serious way, like begging for a favor or for mercy. Daniel was doing this toward his God.
Small leather boxes holding tiny scrolls with Bible verses written on them. Jews tied one to the forehead and one to the left arm, and making them bigger helped people notice them.
A poultice is a soft, mushy mixture, like one made from bread or bran, that is spread on a sore or swollen part of the body to help it heal.
Principalities are a kind of spiritual being, an order of angels, good or bad. Paul names them in this verse alongside angels and powers.
Reconciling means bringing people back into friendship after they have been enemies. Here, God was making peace between Himself and people through Christ, so they could be close to Him again.
A reviler is someone who insults another person or speaks to that person in a rude, disrespectful way.
To revile someone is to say mean, insulting words to them or about them. In this verse, the wicked man speaks badly about the LORD and shows Him no respect.
Rites are special acts of worship that people do in a set way, following a rule or a long-time custom. They are formal ceremonies, like the Jewish rites of purification in this verse.
A Scythian was someone from the wandering herding tribes of the far lands above two big seas, the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea. Many people of that time saw them as rough and uneducated.
The Sepharvites were the people who lived in Sepharvaim. They are named in 2 Kings 17.
The Shechemites were the family of Shechem, a group of people who belonged to his family line.
Sheshach is a secret, code name for Babylon. It is used only in Jeremiah, where it stands in place of the name of that city or land.
In this verse, "Sheth" is probably not a person's name. It likely means "tumult," so "sons of Sheth" would mean people of noise and trouble, who are struck down.
A Hebrew word meaning a stream or an ear of grain. The Gileadites used it as a test, since the Ephraimites said "sibboleth" and could not make the "sh" sound.
A word in a psalm's title, probably meaning a wild, emotional song or poem sung with music, maybe a sad one. No one knows its exact meaning today.
Shigionoth is probably a music word. It likely tells how the prayer of Habakkuk was meant to be set to music or sung.
The name of the parent of Jehozabad, one of the servants who killed King Joash. In 2 Chronicles 24:26 the name is given as Shimrith, and it means "keeper" or "watchman."
Sivan was a month in the Jewish calendar, the third one of the year. It fell in late spring and early summer, around May and June.
Sonship is the state of being a son, having the relationship of a son to a father.
Soothsaying is telling what will happen in the future without God's help or authority. It is different from true prophecy.
A sorceress is a woman who practices magic or casts spells. She is a female magician or enchantress.
Sorrel describes a reddish-brown color, often used for a horse's coat. In this verse, it names the color of one group of horses.
A supplication is a prayer or request made with deep feeling, where a person asks with a gentle, sincere heart and really means it. It can be part of worship.
Tammuz was a false god of ancient peoples, whose name means "Sprout of Life." He was linked to growing things, and worshippers cried loudly in sadness at a yearly festival for him.
Tebeth was the name the Jews used for their tenth month, which falls around December and January. Its name may come from an old word for the cold part of the year.
A thresher is a person who thrashes grain, which means beating it, or a machine that does this job. In this verse, it is a worker who helps with the harvest.
A Timnite is a man of Timnah. In the Bible, this word is used for Samson's father-in-law, the father of his wife.
Vanity means something empty that has nothing real inside to satisfy. In this verse it is what people foolishly chase, which gives no real good and leaves them wanting more.
Vinedressers are workers who take care of grapevines. They trim the vines and help them grow in a vineyard.
Witchcraft is the evil practice of pretending to have secret powers, such as telling the future or speaking with spirits. The Bible strongly speaks against it.
